bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑第182卷卷第一百八十二

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror to Aid in Government, Volume 182, scroll number one hundred eighty-two.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 182.

sentences.zh: 【隋紀六】起昭陽作噩，盡旃蒙大淵獻，凡三年。

translations.literal: [Sui Records 6] From Zhaoyang Zuoe through Zhanmeng Dayuanxian, three years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Records of Sui, Number Six] Spanning from the cyclical year Zhaoyang Zuoe through Zhanmeng Dayuanxian—three years in all.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丁丑，詔徵天下兵集涿郡。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, day dingchou: an edict was issued to levy troops from throughout the realm to assemble at Zhuo commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the dingchou day of the first month, an edict ordered troops from across the empire to gather at Zhuo commandery.

sentences.zh: 始募民為驍果，修遼東古城以貯軍糧。

translations.literal: For the first time commoners were recruited as Xiaoguo, and old cities in Liaodong were repaired to store military grain.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners were first enlisted as the Xiaoguo corps, and abandoned cities in Liaodong were restored to hold army provisions.

sentences.zh: 靈武賊帥白瑜娑劫掠牧馬，北連突厥，隴右多被其患，謂之「奴賊」。

translations.literal: The bandit chieftain Bai Yusa of Lingwu raided government horses, allied with the Turks in the north, and Longyou suffered greatly from him—they called him the "Slave Bandit."
translations.idiomatic: Bai Yusa, a rebel leader in Lingwu, plundered imperial stud herds and allied with the Turks to the north; Longyou was ravaged by his raids, and people called him the Slave Bandit.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，赦天下。

translations.literal: On day wuxu, an amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuxu day, the emperor proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 己亥，命刑部尚書衛文升等輔代王侑留守西京。

translations.literal: On day jihai, Wei Wensheng, Minister of Justice, and others were ordered to assist the Prince of Dai, You, in remaining to guard the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the jihai day, the emperor appointed Minister of Justice Wei Wensheng and others to support Prince Dai You in holding the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 二月，壬午，詔：「宇文述以兵糧不繼，遂陷王師；

translations.literal: Second month, day renwu, an edict: "Yuwen Shu, because military grain did not keep up, caused the royal army to fall into disaster;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the renwu day, an edict declared: "Because army provisions failed to arrive in time, Yuwen Shu brought disaster upon the imperial forces;

sentences.zh: 乃軍吏失於支料，非述之罪，宜復其官爵。」

translations.literal: yet it was the army clerks who failed in dispensing supplies, not Shu's crime—his rank and titles should be restored."
translations.idiomatic: yet the fault lay with supply clerks who mismanaged disbursements, not with Shu himself—his offices and titles should be restored."

sentences.zh: 尋又加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was additionally appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Honored Equipage, Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was further promoted to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Honored Equipage of the Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 帝謂侍臣曰：「高麗小虜，侮慢上國；

translations.literal: The Emperor said to his attendants: "Goguryeo is a petty frontier foe that insults our great state;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his attendants: "Goguryeo is a trifling border state that dares slight our empire;

sentences.zh: 今拔海移山，猶望克果，況此虜乎！」

translations.literal: now if we can move seas and shift mountains and still hope to succeed, how much more this petty foe!"
translations.idiomatic: if we can drain seas and move mountains and still expect success, how much more so against this petty enemy!"

sentences.zh: 乃復議伐高麗。

translations.literal: Thereupon they again deliberated on campaigning against Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the court again debated war against Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 左光祿大夫郭榮諫曰：「戎狄失禮，臣下之事；

translations.literal: Left Grand Master for Promoting Righteousness Guo Rong remonstrated: "When the barbarians lose decorum, that is a matter for subordinates;
translations.idiomatic: Left Grand Master for Promoting Righteousness Guo Rong admonished: "When frontier peoples breach protocol, that is work for officials below;

sentences.zh: 千鈞之弩，不為鼷鼠發機，奈何親辱萬乘以敵小寇乎！」

translations.literal: a crossbow of a thousand jun does not release its mechanism for a xishu rat—why should the Son of Heaven personally humiliate the imperial chariot to fight a petty bandit?"
translations.idiomatic: a thousand-jun crossbow is not drawn for a field mouse—why should Your Majesty personally debase the imperial presence to meet a petty raider?"

sentences.zh: 帝不聽。

translations.literal: The Emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused to heed him.

sentences.zh: 三月，丙子，濟陰孟海公起為盜，保據周橋，眾至數萬，見人稱引書史，輒殺之。

translations.literal: Third month, day bingzi, Meng Haigong of Jiyin rose as a bandit, seized and held Zhouqiao, his followers reached tens of thousands; whenever he saw someone cite books and histories, he would kill them.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the bingzi day, Meng Haigong of Jiyin took to banditry, fortified Zhouqiao, and gathered tens of thousands; anyone he heard quoting books or history he killed on the spot.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，發丁男十萬城大興。

translations.literal: Day dingchou: one hundred thousand able-bodied men were drafted to fortify Daxing.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingchou day, one hundred thousand conscripted men were sent to build up the walls of Daxing.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，帝幸遼東，命民部尚書樊子蓋等輔越王侗留守東都。

translations.literal: Day wuyin: the Emperor went to Liaodong and ordered Minister of Revenue Fan Zigai and others to assist the Prince of Yue, Tong, in remaining to guard the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuyin day the emperor departed for Liaodong and left Minister of Revenue Fan Zigai and others to support Prince Yue Tong in holding the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 時所在盜起，齊郡王薄、孟讓、北海郭方預、清河張金稱、平原郝孝德、河間格謙、勃海孫宣雅，各聚眾攻剽，多者十餘萬，少者數萬人，山東苦之。

translations.literal: At that time bandits rose everywhere; Wang Bo of Qi commandery, Meng Rang, Guo Fangyu of Beihai, Zhang Jincheng of Qinghe, Hao Xiaode of Pingyuan, Ge Qian of Hejian, and Sun Xuanya of Bohai each gathered followers to raid—they numbered over one hundred thousand at most and tens of thousands at least, and Shandong suffered terribly.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits were rising everywhere: Wang Bo of Qi, Meng Rang, Guo Fangyu of Beihai, Zhang Jincheng of Qinghe, Hao Xiaode of Pingyuan, Ge Qian of Hejian, and Sun Xuanya of Bohai each mustered gangs for plunder—some above a hundred thousand, none fewer than tens of thousands—and Shandong groaned under the scourge.

sentences.zh: 天下承平日久，人不習兵，郡縣吏每與賊戰，望風沮敗。

translations.literal: The realm had long been at peace, and people were unused to warfare; whenever county and prefectural officials fought the bandits, they would break and flee at the first sight of the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: After generations of peace the people knew nothing of war; whenever local officials met the rebels they usually broke and fled at the first alarm.

sentences.zh: 唯齊郡丞閺鄉張須陀得士眾心，勇決善戰，將郡兵擊王薄於泰山下。

translations.literal: Only Zhang Sotuo, assistant magistrate of Qi commandery from Minxiang, won the hearts of his soldiers, was resolute and brave in battle, and led the commandery troops to attack Wang Bo below Mount Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Only Zhang Sotuo, assistant magistrate of Qi from Minxiang, won the loyalty of his men; bold and skilled in battle, he led the commandery forces against Wang Bo at the foot of Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: 薄恃其驟勝，不設備；

translations.literal: Bo relied on his sudden victories and made no preparations;
translations.idiomatic: Bo, trusting in his string of quick victories, took no precautions;

sentences.zh: 須陀掩擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Sotuo launched a surprise attack and utterly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Sotuo struck by surprise and routed him completely.

sentences.zh: 薄收餘兵北渡河，須陀追擊於臨邑，又破之。

translations.literal: Bo gathered his remaining troops and fled north across the Yellow River; Sotuo pursued him to Linyi and defeated him again.
translations.idiomatic: Bo rallied his survivors and fled north across the Yellow River; Sotuo pursued him to Linyi and defeated him once more.

sentences.zh: 薄北連孫宣雅、郝孝德等十餘萬攻章丘，須陀帥步騎二萬擊之，賊眾大敗。

translations.literal: Bo allied north with Sun Xuanya, Hao Xiaode, and more than one hundred thousand men to attack Zhangqiu; Sotuo led twenty thousand infantry and cavalry to attack them, and the bandit host was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Bo then joined Sun Xuanya, Hao Xiaode, and others—more than a hundred thousand in all—to assault Zhangqiu; Sotuo led twenty thousand foot and horse soldiers against them and smashed the rebel host.

sentences.zh: 賊帥裴長才等眾二萬掩至城下，大掠。

translations.literal: The bandit chieftain Pei Changcai and others, twenty thousand strong, came by surprise to below the city and looted extensively.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit leader Pei Changcai and twenty thousand men suddenly appeared beneath the walls and plundered freely.

sentences.zh: 須陀未暇集兵，帥五騎與戰，賊競赴之，圍百餘重，身中數創，勇氣彌厲。

translations.literal: Sotuo had no time to gather troops; he led five horsemen into battle; the bandits all rushed at him and surrounded him in more than a hundred layers; he received several wounds, yet his valor grew fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: Sotuo had no chance to muster his force; he charged in with only five horsemen. The rebels swarmed him in layer upon layer of encirclement; though he took many wounds, his fighting spirit only burned hotter.

sentences.zh: 會城中兵至，賊稍退卻。

translations.literal: When the troops in the city arrived, the bandits drew back somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: When reinforcements from the city arrived, the rebels fell back a little.

sentences.zh: 須陀督眾擊之，長才等敗走。

translations.literal: Sotuo urged his men forward to attack; Changcai and the others fled in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Sotuo rallied his men and pressed the attack; Changcai and his band fled in defeat.

sentences.zh: 庚子，郭方預等合軍攻陷北海，大掠而去。

translations.literal: Day gengzi: Guo Fangyu and others combined armies, captured and overran Beihai, looted extensively, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengzi day, Guo Fangyu and allied bands stormed Beihai, plundered the city, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 須陀謂民屬曰：「賊恃其強，謂我不能救。

translations.literal: Sotuo said to the people: "The bandits rely on their strength and think we cannot save you.
translations.idiomatic: Sotuo told the townspeople: "The rebels trust in their numbers and believe we cannot rescue you.

sentences.zh: 吾今速行，破之必矣！」

translations.literal: If we march swiftly now, we are sure to break them!"
translations.idiomatic: If we march at once, we are certain to crush them!"

sentences.zh: 乃簡精兵倍道進擊，大破之，斬數萬級，前後獲賊輜重不可勝計。

translations.literal: Thereupon he selected elite troops and advanced by forced marches to attack, utterly defeating them, beheading tens of thousands; before and after, bandit booty taken was beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: He then picked elite troops, marched by forced stages, and smashed the enemy, taking tens of thousands of heads; rebel baggage captured before and after was beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 歷城羅士信，年十四，從須陀擊賊於濰水上。

translations.literal: Luo Shixin of Licheng, aged fourteen, followed Sotuo to attack bandits on the Wei River.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shixin of Licheng, only fourteen years old, followed Sotuo to fight bandits along the Wei River.

sentences.zh: 賊始布陳，士信馳至陳前，刺殺數人，斬一人首，擲空中，以槊盛之，揭以略陳；

translations.literal: When the bandits had just deployed their formation, Shixin galloped to the front of the formation, stabbed and killed several men, cut off one man's head, tossed it into the air, caught it on his spear, and raised it aloft along the lines;
translations.idiomatic: As the rebels were forming their battle line, Shixin galloped to the fore, killed several men in succession, severed one head, tossed it skyward, caught it on his spear, and paraded it along the enemy ranks;

sentences.zh: 賊徒愕眙，莫敢近。

translations.literal: The bandits were stunned and dared not approach.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel ranks stood frozen in shock; none dared close with him.

sentences.zh: 須陀因引兵奮擊，賊眾大潰。

translations.literal: Sotuo thereupon led the troops in a fierce assault, and the bandit host was utterly routed.
translations.idiomatic: Sotuo then drove his men forward in a fierce charge, and the rebel host collapsed in rout.

sentences.zh: 士信逐北，每殺一人，劓其鼻懷之，還，以驗殺賊之數；

translations.literal: Shixin pursued northward; for each man he killed he cut off the nose and carried it in his bosom; on returning, he used them to verify the number of bandits killed;
translations.idiomatic: Shixin pursued the fleeing enemy; for each man he slew he cut off the nose and tucked it in his robe, then on returning counted them to prove how many rebels he had killed;

sentences.zh: 須陀歎賞，引置左右。

translations.literal: Sotuo sighed in admiration and kept him at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Sotuo marveled at his deed and kept him at his side.

sentences.zh: 每戰，須陀先登，士信為副。

translations.literal: In every battle Sotuo would charge first; Shixin served as his second.
translations.idiomatic: In every fight Sotuo led the assault and Shixin followed as his second.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使慰諭，並畫須陀、士信戰陳之狀而觀之。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent envoys to console and commend them, and had pictures painted of Sotuo and Shixin in battle for him to view.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys with words of praise and had paintings made of Sotuo and Shixin in battle for his own viewing.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，庚午，車駕渡遼。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day gengwu: the imperial carriage crossed the Liao.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, on the gengwu day of the fourth month, the imperial procession crossed the Liao River.

sentences.zh: 壬申，遣宇文述與上大將軍楊義臣趣平壤。

translations.literal: Day renshen: Yuwen Shu and Senior General-in-Chief Yang Yichen were sent to press on toward Pyongyang.
translations.idiomatic: On the renshen day, Yuwen Shu and Senior General-in-Chief Yang Yichen were dispatched to advance on Pyongyang.

sentences.zh: 左光祿大夫王仁恭出扶餘道。

translations.literal: Left Grand Master for Promoting Righteousness Wang Rengong advanced by the Fuyu route.
translations.idiomatic: Left Grand Master for Promoting Righteousness Wang Rengong marched out by the Fuyu route.

sentences.zh: 仁恭進軍至新城，高麗兵數萬拒戰，仁恭帥勁騎一千擊破之，高麗嬰城固守。

translations.literal: Rengong advanced his army to Xincheng; tens of thousands of Goguryeo troops resisted in battle; Rengong led a thousand crack cavalry to attack and break them; Goguryeo held the walls and would not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Rengong marched to Xincheng, where tens of thousands of Goguryeo soldiers met him in battle; he led a thousand elite horsemen to shatter them, after which the enemy shut themselves within the walls and refused to sally forth.

sentences.zh: 帝命諸將攻遼東，聽以便宜從事。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered the generals to attack Liaodong, allowing them to act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered his generals to assault Liaodong and granted them discretion to act as local conditions demanded.

sentences.zh: 飛樓、橦、雲梯、地道四面俱進，晝夜不息，而高麗應變拒之，二十餘日不拔，主客死者甚眾。

translations.literal: Flying towers, battering rams, cloud ladders, and sapping tunnels advanced from all four sides day and night without cease, but Goguryeo met each change and resisted; for more than twenty days they could not take it, and attackers and defenders alike died in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Flying towers, battering rams, siege ladders, and mining tunnels pressed in from every side without pause day or night, yet Goguryeo adapted and held them off; after more than twenty days the city still stood, and both besiegers and defenders fell in vast numbers.

sentences.zh: 沖梯竿長十五丈，驍果吳興沈光升其端，臨城與高麗戰，短兵接，殺十數人，高麗競擊之而墜；

translations.literal: Assault ladders with poles fifteen zhang long—the fierce warrior Shen Guang of Wuxing climbed to the top, fought Goguryeo at the wall with short weapons, killed more than ten men; Goguryeo massed to strike him and he fell;
translations.idiomatic: On assault ladders whose poles were fifteen zhang high, the Xiaoguo fighter Shen Guang of Wuxing climbed to the top, fought hand to hand atop the wall, and killed more than ten men before the Goguryeo troops swarmed him and knocked him down;

sentences.zh: 未及地，適遇竿有垂絲亙，光接而復上。

translations.literal: Before he reached the ground, a dangling rope happened to span the pole; Guang caught it and climbed up again.
translations.idiomatic: Before he hit the ground a loose rope happened to hang across the pole; Guang seized it and hauled himself back up.

sentences.zh: 帝望見，壯之，即拜朝散大夫，恆置左右。

translations.literal: When the Emperor saw this from afar he admired his valor and immediately appointed him Gentleman Consultant for the Court, keeping him always at his side.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw this from afar, admired his daring, and at once appointed him Gentleman Consultant for the Court, keeping him constantly at hand.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書楊玄感，驍勇，便騎射，好讀書，喜賓客，海內知名之士多與之遊；

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Yang Xuangan was brave and fierce, skilled at mounted archery, fond of reading, and delighted in entertaining guests; many renowned men throughout the realm associated with him;
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Yang Xuangan was fierce in battle, expert at mounted archery, devoted to books, and fond of hosting guests; many celebrated men across the realm sought his company;

sentences.zh: 與薄山公李密善。

translations.literal: He was on close terms with Li Mi, Duke of Boshan.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially close to Li Mi, Duke of Boshan.

sentences.zh: 密，弼之曾孫也，少有才略，志氣雄遠，輕財好士，為左親侍。

translations.literal: Mi was the great-grandson of Li Bi; in youth he had talent and stratagem, lofty ambition, scorned wealth and cherished scholars, and served as Left Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Mi was the great-grandson of Li Bi; even as a youth he showed talent and strategy, ambition that reached far, generosity toward scholars, and held the post of Left Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 帝見之，謂宇文述曰：「向者左仗下黑色小兒，瞻視異常，勿令宿衛！」

translations.literal: When the Emperor saw him he said to Yuwen Shu: "That small dark boy to the left of the halberd guard looked at things strangely—do not let him serve in the inner guard!"
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor noticed him he told Yuwen Shu: "That dark-complexioned boy beside the left halberd guard stared about in an odd way—do not let him stand night watch in the palace!"

sentences.zh: 述乃諷密使稱病自免，密遂屏人事，專務讀書。

translations.literal: Shu thereupon hinted to Mi to claim illness and resign; Mi then withdrew from worldly affairs and devoted himself to reading.
translations.idiomatic: Shu then prompted Mi to plead illness and resign; Mi withdrew from court life and devoted himself wholly to study.

sentences.zh: 嘗乘黃牛讀《漢書》，楊素遇而異之，因召至家，與語，大悅，謂其子玄感等曰：「李密識度如此，汝等不及也！」

translations.literal: Once, riding an ox and reading the Book of Han, he was noticed by Yang Su, who found him remarkable, summoned him to his house, and spoke with him—was greatly pleased, and told his sons Xuangan and the others: "Li Mi's discernment is like this; you cannot match him!"
translations.idiomatic: Once, reading the Book of Han while riding an ox, he was seen by Yang Su, who was struck by the sight, invited him home, and talked with him at length. Delighted, Su told his sons Xuangan and the rest: "Li Mi's breadth of mind is like this—you are not his equal!"

sentences.zh: 由是玄感與為深交。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xuangan formed a deep friendship with him.
translations.idiomatic: From that time Xuangan became his close friend.

sentences.zh: 時或侮之，密曰：「人言當指實，寧可面諛！

translations.literal: Sometimes people would insult him; Mi said: "When people speak, it should point to what is real—had I rather be flattered to one's face!
translations.idiomatic: When people sometimes slighted him, Mi would say: "Speech should aim at truth—who would choose flattery to one's face!

sentences.zh: 若決機兩陳之間，暗嗚咄嗟，使敵人震懾，密不如公；

translations.literal: But if decisive counsel is needed between two battle lines, or sudden commands snapped out, making the enemy tremble, I am not your equal;
translations.idiomatic: But if the moment calls for a decision between two battle lines, or a sudden shout that makes the enemy quake, I am not your equal;

sentences.zh: 驅策天下賢俊，各申其用，公不如密：豈可以階級稍崇而輕天下士大夫邪！」

translations.literal: to drive and employ worthy men under heaven, each to use his ability—you are not Mi's equal: how can you slight the scholars of the realm just because your rank rises a little!"
translations.idiomatic: to rally the worthy of the realm and set each to his proper use—you are not my equal: can you despise the empire's scholars merely because your rank has risen a little!"

sentences.zh: 玄感笑而服之。

translations.literal: Xuangan smiled and was convinced.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan laughed and accepted it.

sentences.zh: 素恃功驕倨，朝宴之際，或失臣禮。

translations.literal: Su relied on his merit and was proud and disrespectful; at imperial banquets he sometimes failed in a minister's propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Su, trusting in his achievements, grew arrogant; at court banquets he sometimes forgot the deference owed a subject.

sentences.zh: 帝心銜而不言，素亦覺之。

translations.literal: The Emperor harbored resentment but said nothing; Su too perceived it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor nursed resentment but kept silent; Su sensed it as well.

sentences.zh: 及素薨，帝謂近臣曰：「使素不死，終當夷族。」

translations.literal: When Su died the Emperor told close attendants: "If Su had not died, his clan would eventually have been exterminated."
translations.idiomatic: When Su died the emperor told his close attendants: "Had Su lived on, his whole clan would eventually have been wiped out."

sentences.zh: 玄感頗知之，且自以累世貴顯，在朝文武多父之故吏，見朝政日紊，而帝多猜忌，內不自安，乃與諸弟潛謀作亂。

translations.literal: Xuangan understood this quite well; moreover, seeing his own family's generations of eminence, with many in court civil and military being his father's old subordinates, observing daily disorder in court and the Emperor's growing suspicion, he was ill at ease within and secretly plotted rebellion with his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan understood this all too well. He saw his family's generations of power, with many officials at court still his father's old retainers; he watched government grow daily more chaotic and the emperor grow daily more suspicious, and inwardly he could not rest—so he and his brothers secretly plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 帝方事征伐，玄感自言：「世荷國恩，願為將領。」

translations.literal: The Emperor was then engaged in campaigns; Xuangan himself said: "My family has long received the state's grace; I wish to serve as a general."
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor was busy with campaigns, Xuangan volunteered: "My house has long enjoyed the state's favor; I wish to serve as a commander."

sentences.zh: 帝喜曰：「將門必有將，相門必有相，固不虛也！」

translations.literal: The Emperor was pleased and said: "A general's house must produce generals, a minister's house must produce ministers—it is no empty saying!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and said: "A general's house breeds generals, a minister's house breeds ministers—the old saying is true!"

sentences.zh: 由是寵遇日隆，頗預朝政。

translations.literal: Thereupon his favor grew daily and he took part in court policy.
translations.idiomatic: From then on his favor grew daily and he took an active part in state affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝伐高麗，命玄感於黎陽督運，遂與虎賁郎將王仲伯、汲郡贊治趙懷義等謀，故逗遛漕運，不時進發，欲令渡遼諸軍乏食；

translations.literal: When the Emperor campaigned against Goguryeo he ordered Xuangan to supervise transport at Liyang; Xuangan then plotted with Tiger Guards Regiment Commander Wang Zhongbo, Zanzhì Zhao Huaiyi of Ji commandery, and others, deliberately delaying grain transport and not sending it forward on time, intending to make the armies across the Liao lack food;
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor marched on Goguryeo he put Xuangan in charge of grain transport at Liyang; Xuangan then conspired with Tiger Guards Regiment Commander Wang Zhongbo, Ji commandery magistrate Zhao Huaiyi, and others to hold back the canal shipments and send them forward late, so that the armies across the Liao would run short of food;

sentences.zh: 帝遣使者促之，玄感揚言水路多盜，不可前後而發。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent envoys to urge him; Xuangan claimed there were many bandits on the water route and they could not set out front and rear together.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys to hurry him along; Xuangan spread word that bandits infested the waterways and convoys could not travel together in column.

sentences.zh: 玄感弟虎賁郎將玄縱，鷹揚郎將萬石，並從幸遼東，玄感潛遣人召之，二人皆亡還。

translations.literal: Xuangan's younger brothers, Tiger Guards Regiment Commander Xuanganzong and Eagle-Flying Regiment Commander Wanshi, both accompanied the Emperor to Liaodong; Xuangan secretly sent men to summon them, and both fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan's brothers Xuanganzong, a Tiger Guards regiment commander, and Wanshi, an Eagle-Flying regiment commander, were both with the emperor in Liaodong; Xuangan secretly summoned them, and both deserted and fled home.

sentences.zh: 萬石至高陽，為監事許華所執，斬於涿郡。

translations.literal: Wanshi reached Gaoyang, was seized by surveillance officer Xu Hua, and executed at Zhuo commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wanshi reached Gaoyang, was seized by surveillance officer Xu Hua, and beheaded at Zhuo commandery.

sentences.zh: 時右驍衛大將軍來護兒以舟師自東萊將入海趣平壤，玄感遣家奴偽為使者從東方來，詐稱護兒反。

translations.literal: At that time Senior General of the Right Brave Guards Lai Huer led a fleet from Donglai to enter the sea and press toward Pyongyang; Xuangan sent a household slave disguised as an envoy from the east, falsely claiming Huer had rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Senior General of the Right Brave Guards Lai Huer was leading a fleet from Donglai to strike Pyongyang by sea; Xuangan sent a household slave disguised as an envoy from the east to spread a false report that Huer had rebelled.

sentences.zh: 六月，乙巳，玄感入黎陽，閉城，大索男夫，取帆布為牟、甲，署官屬，皆准開皇之舊。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day yisi: Xuangan entered Liyang, closed the city, conscripted men on a large scale, took sailcloth for mantlets and armor, appointed officials—all according to the Kaihuang precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the yisi day, Xuangan entered Liyang, shut the gates, pressed every able-bodied man into service, took sailcloth for mantlets and armor, and appointed officials—all on the Kaihuang model.

sentences.zh: 移書傍郡，以討護兒為名，各令發兵會於倉所。

translations.literal: He sent letters to neighboring commanderies in the name of punishing Huer, each ordering troops to assemble at the granary.
translations.idiomatic: He sent proclamations to neighboring commanderies in the name of punishing Huer, ordering each to raise troops and assemble at the granary depot.

sentences.zh: 郡縣官有干用者，玄感皆以運糧追集之，以趙懷義為衛州刺史，東光尉元務本為黎州刺史，河內郡主簿唐禕為懷州刺史。

translations.literal: County and prefectural officials who were capable he all summoned by pursuing grain transport; he made Zhao Huaiyi Inspector of Weizhou, Yuan Wuben of Dongguang Assistant Magistrate of Liyang, and Tang Yi of Henei chief clerk Inspector of Huaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Capable local officials he rounded up under the pretext of grain transport; he made Zhao Huaiyi inspector of Weizhou, Yuan Wuben of Dongguang inspector of Liyang, and Tang Yi, chief clerk of Henei, inspector of Huaizhou.

sentences.zh: 治書侍御史游元，督運在黎陽，玄感謂曰：「獨夫肆虐，陷身絕域，此天亡之時也。

translations.literal: Investigative Censor You Yuan, who was supervising transport at Liyang—Xuangan said to him: "The tyrant ravages cruelly and plunges himself into a remote land—this is the hour of Heaven's destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Investigative Censor You Yuan was supervising transport at Liyang when Xuangan said to him: "The tyrant rages unchecked and has trapped himself in a distant land—this is the hour Heaven has chosen for his fall.

sentences.zh: 我今親帥義兵以誅無道，卿意如何？」

translations.literal: I now personally lead righteous troops to punish the lawless—what is your wish?"
translations.idiomatic: I now lead righteous troops in person to punish the lawless—what say you?"

sentences.zh: 元正色曰：「尊公荷國寵靈，近古無比。

translations.literal: Yuan said sternly: "Your honored father received the state's favor and distinction, unmatched in recent ages.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan answered sternly: "Your father enjoyed the state's favor beyond compare in recent memory.

sentences.zh: 公之弟兄，青紫交映，當謂竭誠盡節上答鴻恩。

translations.literal: You and your brothers, court robes and seals bright together—you should have devoted loyalty and utmost integrity to repay the great grace.
translations.idiomatic: You and your brothers wear high office one upon another—you should repay that vast grace with utmost loyalty.

sentences.zh: 豈意墳土未干，親圖反噬！

translations.literal: Who would have thought that before your father's tomb was dry you would plot treachery against your kin!
translations.idiomatic: Who would have thought that before your father's grave was dry you would turn on the state that raised you!

sentences.zh: 僕有死而己，不敢聞命！」

translations.literal: I have but death—that I dare not obey your command!"
translations.idiomatic: I have only death to offer—I will not heed your command!"

sentences.zh: 玄感怒而囚之，屢脅以兵，不能屈，乃殺之。

translations.literal: Xuangan was angry and imprisoned him; repeatedly threatened him with weapons but could not bend him, and thereupon killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan flew into a rage and imprisoned him; he threatened him again and again with arms but could not break him, and in the end had him killed.

sentences.zh: 元，明根之孫也。

translations.literal: Yuan was the grandson of You Minggen.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was a grandson of You Minggen.

sentences.zh: 玄感選運夫少壯者得五千餘人，丹楊、宣城篙梢三千餘人，刑三牲誓眾，且諭之曰：「主上無道，不以百姓為念，天下騷擾，死遼東者以萬計。

translations.literal: Xuangan selected more than five thousand able-bodied grain carriers and more than three thousand boatmen from Danyang and Xuancheng, slaughtered three sacrificial animals to swear the host, and addressed them: "The lord above is without the Way, heedless of the common people; the realm is in turmoil and those who died in Liaodong number in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan picked out more than five thousand able-bodied transport laborers and more than three thousand boatmen from Danyang and Xuancheng, sacrificed three animals to bind the host by oath, and told them: "The ruler is without the Way and cares nothing for the people; the realm is in turmoil, and those who have died in Liaodong number in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 今與君等起兵，以救兆民之弊，何如？」

translations.literal: Now I join with you to raise troops to save the masses from their affliction—what say you?"
translations.idiomatic: Now I join with you to raise arms and deliver the people from their misery—what say you?"

sentences.zh: 眾皆踴躍稱萬歲。

translations.literal: The crowd all leaped up and shouted "Long live!"
translations.idiomatic: The crowd leaped up as one and shouted "Long live!"

sentences.zh: 乃勒兵部分。

translations.literal: He then marshaled troops and assigned divisions.
translations.idiomatic: He then arrayed the troops and assigned their divisions.

sentences.zh: 唐禕自玄感所逃歸河內。

translations.literal: Tang Yi escaped from Xuangan's place and returned to Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Yi fled from Xuangan's camp and made his way back to Henei.

sentences.zh: 先是玄感陰遣家僮至長安，召李密及弟玄挺赴黎陽。

translations.literal: Earlier Xuangan had secretly sent household slaves to Chang'an to summon Li Mi and his younger brother Xuanting to Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Xuangan had secretly sent household servants to Chang'an to summon Li Mi and his brother Xuanting to Liyang.

sentences.zh: 及舉兵，密適至，玄感大喜，以為謀主，謂密曰：「子常以濟物為己任，今其時矣！

translations.literal: When he raised troops Mi had just arrived; Xuangan was greatly pleased and made him chief strategist, saying to Mi: "You have always taken saving the world as your charge—now is the time!
translations.idiomatic: When the rebellion broke out Mi had just arrived; Xuangan was overjoyed, made him his chief strategist, and said: "You have always made saving the world your task—now is the moment!

sentences.zh: 計將安出？」

translations.literal: What plan do you propose?"
translations.idiomatic: What is your plan?"

sentences.zh: 密曰：「天子出征，遠在遼外，去幽州猶隔千里。

translations.literal: Mi said: "The Son of Heaven is on campaign, far off in Liaodong, a thousand li from Youzhou still.
translations.idiomatic: Mi said: "The Son of Heaven is on campaign, far away in Liaodong, still a thousand li from Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 南有巨海，北有強胡，中間一道，理極艱危。

translations.literal: To the south lies a vast sea, to the north strong Hu; in between one road—extremely perilous in principle.
translations.idiomatic: To the south lies the open sea, to the north fierce barbarians; between them a single road—by its nature desperately perilous.

sentences.zh: 公擁兵出其不意，長驅入薊，據臨渝之險，扼其咽喉。

translations.literal: If you lead troops by surprise, drive straight into Ji, seize the peril at Linyu ford and choke his throat.
translations.idiomatic: If you lead your forces by surprise, drive straight into Ji, hold the perilous crossing at Linyu, and seize his throat.

sentences.zh: 歸路既絕，高麗聞之，必躡其後。

translations.literal: Once the road home is cut, Goguryeo hearing it will surely tread on his heels.
translations.idiomatic: Once his line of retreat is cut, Goguryeo will hear of it and surely press on his rear.

sentences.zh: 不過旬月，資糧皆盡，其眾不降則潰，可不戰而擒，此上計也。」

translations.literal: Within no more than a month or so grain will all be gone; if his host does not surrender it will scatter—you can capture him without fighting; this is the supreme plan."
translations.idiomatic: Within a month or so his supplies will be exhausted; his army will either surrender or scatter—you can take him without a battle. That is the best plan."

sentences.zh: 玄感曰：「更言其次。」

translations.literal: Xuangan said: "Speak the next plan."
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan said: "Tell me the next plan."

sentences.zh: 密曰：「關中四塞，天府之國，雖有衛文升，不足為意。

translations.literal: Mi said: "Within the passes are four barriers, a treasury of the realm; though there is Wei Wensheng, he is no concern.
translations.idiomatic: Mi said: "The Guanzhong region is locked by four passes—a natural treasury of the realm; though Wei Wensheng is there, he need not trouble you.

sentences.zh: 今帥眾鼓行而西，經城勿攻，直取長安。

translations.literal: Now lead the host with drums marching west, pass cities without attacking, take Chang'an directly.
translations.idiomatic: Now march your army west with drums beating; do not stop to attack the cities you pass, but drive straight for Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 收其豪傑，撫其士民，據險而守之。

translations.literal: Gather its talented men, comfort its scholars and people, hold perilous places and defend them.
translations.idiomatic: Win over its outstanding men, reassure its gentry and common people, and hold the strategic strongpoints.

sentences.zh: 天子雖還，失其根本，可徐圖也。」

translations.literal: Though the Son of Heaven returns, he loses his root foundation; one can plan slowly."
translations.idiomatic: Even if the emperor returns, he will have lost his base—then you can pursue your aims at leisure."

sentences.zh: 玄感曰：「更言其次。」

translations.literal: Xuangan said: "Speak the next plan."
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan said: "Tell me the next plan."

sentences.zh: 密曰：「簡精銳，晝夜倍道，襲取東都，以號令四方。

translations.literal: Mi said: "Select elite troops, day and night double the march, surprise and take the Eastern Capital, to issue commands to the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Mi said: "Pick elite troops, force-march day and night, strike and seize the Eastern Capital, and from there command the realm.

sentences.zh: 但恐唐禕告之，先己固守。

translations.literal: But I fear Tang Yi will report it, and they will fortify and hold first.
translations.idiomatic: But I fear Tang Yi will get word and they will fortify the city before we arrive.

sentences.zh: 若引兵攻之，百日不克，天下之兵四面而至，非僕所知也。」

translations.literal: If we lead troops to attack it, a hundred days without taking it, the realm's armies will arrive from all four sides—this is not what your servant knows how to handle."
translations.idiomatic: If we lay siege, we may fail to take it within a hundred days, and armies from every quarter will converge—I cannot foresee how that ends."

sentences.zh: 玄感曰：「不然，今百官家口並在東都，若先取之，足以動其心。

translations.literal: Xuangan said: "Not so. Now all the officials' families are in the Eastern Capital; if we take it first, it is enough to move their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan said: "Not so. Every official's family is in the Eastern Capital now; if we seize it first, that alone will shake them.

sentences.zh: 且經城不拔，何以示威！

translations.literal: Moreover, passing cities without taking them—how can we show authority!
translations.idiomatic: Besides, what authority do we show if we pass every city without capturing it!

sentences.zh: 公之下計，乃上策也。」

translations.literal: Sir's lower plan is in truth the upper strategy."
translations.idiomatic: Your lowest plan is actually the best strategy."

sentences.zh: 遂引兵向洛陽，遣楊玄挺將驍勇千人為前鋒，先取河內。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led troops toward Luoyang, sent Yang Xuanting with a thousand fierce warriors as vanguard, first to take Henei.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon marched on Luoyang, sending Yang Xuanting with a thousand crack troops as vanguard to take Henei first.

sentences.zh: 唐禕據城拒守，玄挺無所獲。

translations.literal: Tang Yi held the city and resisted; Xuanting gained nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Yi held the city and refused battle, and Xuanting took nothing.

sentences.zh: 禕又使人告東都越王侗與樊子蓋等勒兵為備，修武民相帥守臨清關。

translations.literal: Yi also sent men to inform the Prince of Yue, Yang Tong, at the Eastern Capital, and Fan Zigai and others to drill troops for defense; the people of Xiuwu led one another to guard Linqing Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Yi also sent word to the Eastern Capital to Prince of Yue Yang Tong and Fan Zigai and the rest to mobilize for defense, and the people of Xiuwu rallied to hold Linqing Pass.

sentences.zh: 玄感不得度，乃於汲郡南渡河，從之者如市。

translations.literal: Xuangan could not cross, so south of Ji Prefecture he crossed the river; followers were like a market crowd.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to get through, Xuangan crossed the river south of Ji Commandery, and followers thronged him like a market crowd.

sentences.zh: 使弟積善將兵三千自偃師南緣洛水西入，玄挺自白司馬板逾邙山南入，玄感將三千餘人隨其後，相去十里許，自稱大軍。

translations.literal: He sent his younger brother Jishan to lead three thousand troops from Yanshi south along the Luo River westward; Xuanting from White Horse Ford crossed Mount Mang southward; Xuangan led more than three thousand men behind them, about ten li apart, calling themselves the great army.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his brother Jishan with three thousand men to enter from the south along the west bank of the Luo from Yanshi; Xuanting crossed Mount Mang from White Horse Ford to the south; Xuangan followed with over three thousand men, the columns about ten li apart, all calling themselves the main force.

sentences.zh: 其兵皆執單刀柳楯，無弓矢甲冑。

translations.literal: Their troops all carried single sabers and willow shields, with no bows, arrows, armor, or helmets.
translations.idiomatic: His soldiers carried only single-edged blades and willow-wood shields—they had no bows, arrows, armor, or helmets.

sentences.zh: 東都遣河南令達奚善意將精兵五千人拒積善，將作監、河南贊治裴弘策將八千人拒玄挺。

translations.literal: The Eastern Capital sent Henan Prefect Daxi Shanyi with five thousand elite troops to oppose Jishan, and Director of Palace Construction and Henan Administrative Supervisor Pei Hongce with eight thousand to oppose Xuanting.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Capital sent Henan Prefect Daxi Shanyi with five thousand elite troops to block Jishan, and Director of Palace Construction and Henan Administrative Supervisor Pei Hongce with eight thousand to block Xuanting.

sentences.zh: 善意渡洛南，營於漢王寺；

translations.literal: Shanyi crossed south of the Luo and encamped at Hanwang Temple;
translations.idiomatic: Shanyi crossed south of the Luo and encamped at Hanwang Temple;

sentences.zh: 明日，積善兵至，不戰自潰，鎧仗皆為積善所取。

translations.literal: The next day Jishan's troops arrived; without fighting they scattered on their own, and armor and weapons were all taken by Jishan.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Jishan's men arrived; Shanyi's force broke without a fight, and Jishan seized all their armor and weapons.

sentences.zh: 弘策出至白司馬板，一戰，敗走，棄鎧仗者太半，玄挺亦不追。

translations.literal: Hongce went out to White Horse Ford, one battle, defeated and fled; more than half abandoned armor and weapons, and Xuanting did not pursue.
translations.idiomatic: Hongce marched out to White Horse Ford; after one engagement he was routed, and more than half his men cast off their armor and arms—Xuanting did not pursue.

sentences.zh: 弘策退三四里，收散兵，復結陳以待之；

translations.literal: Hongce retreated three or four li, gathered scattered troops, and again formed battle lines to wait;
translations.idiomatic: Hongce fell back three or four li, rallied his scattered men, and re-formed his lines to wait;

sentences.zh: 玄挺徐至，坐息良久，忽起擊之，弘策又敗，如是五戰。

translations.literal: Xuanting arrived slowly, sat and rested a long while, then suddenly rose and struck; Hongce was defeated again—so it went for five battles.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanting advanced at an easy pace, rested his men a long while, then suddenly attacked; Hongce was beaten again—this happened five times.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，玄挺直抵太陽門，弘策將士餘騎馳入宮城，自餘無一人返者，皆歸於玄感。

translations.literal: On bingchen Xuanting went straight to the Taiyang Gate; Hongce's officers and soldiers, a few horsemen, galloped into the palace city; of the rest not one returned—all submitted to Xuangan.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen Xuanting reached the Taiyang Gate outright; Hongce and a handful of horsemen raced into the palace city; of the rest not a man came back—they all went over to Xuangan.

sentences.zh: 玄感屯上春門，每誓眾曰：「我身為上柱國，家累鉅萬金，至於富貴，無所求也。

translations.literal: Xuangan encamped at Shangchun Gate; each time he swore to the host, saying: "I personally am a Pillar of State; my family's wealth exceeds tens of thousands in gold—as for riches and honor, I seek nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan encamped at the Upper Spring Gate and often addressed the troops: "I am already a Pillar of the State, and my family's wealth runs to tens of thousands in gold—there is nothing left for me to want in rank or riches.

sentences.zh: 今不顧滅族者，但為天下解倒懸之急耳！」

translations.literal: Now disregarding the extermination of my clan, it is only to relieve the realm's crisis of hanging upside down!"
translations.idiomatic: I risk the destruction of my whole clan only to deliver the realm from its desperate plight!"

sentences.zh: 眾皆悅。

translations.literal: The host all rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: The troops all cheered.

sentences.zh: 父老爭獻牛酒，子弟詣軍門請自效者，日以千數。

translations.literal: Elders competed to offer oxen and wine; sons and younger men came to the army gates asking to serve—their number reached thousands daily.
translations.idiomatic: Local elders vied to bring cattle and wine, and young men came to the gates offering their service by the thousands each day.

sentences.zh: 內史舍人韋福嗣，洸之兄子也，從軍出拒玄感。

translations.literal: Palace Secretariat Attendant Wei Fusi, nephew of Kuang, went with the army to oppose Xuangan.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Secretariat Attendant Wei Fusi, a nephew of Wei Kuang, marched out with the army to resist Xuangan.

sentences.zh: 為玄感所獲；

translations.literal: He was captured by Xuangan;
translations.idiomatic: He was captured by Xuangan;

sentences.zh: 玄感厚禮之，使與其黨胡師耽共掌文翰。

translations.literal: Xuangan treated him generously and had him, with his follower Hu Shidan, jointly manage documents.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan honored him generously and put him in charge of documents together with his follower Hu Shidan.

sentences.zh: 玄感令福嗣為書遺樊子蓋，數帝罪惡，云：「今欲廢昏立明，願勿拘小禮，自貽伊戚。」

translations.literal: Xuangan had Fusi write a letter to Fan Zigai, reciting the emperor's crimes, saying: "Now we wish to remove the benighted and establish the enlightened; please do not cling to petty propriety and bring sorrow on yourselves."
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan had Fusi write to Fan Zigai, listing the emperor's crimes, saying: "We mean now to depose the dark ruler and set up a worthy one—do not let small formalities bind you to self-inflicted ruin."

sentences.zh: 樊子蓋新自外籓入為京官，東都舊官多慢之，至於部分軍事，未甚承稟。

translations.literal: Fan Zigai had newly entered the capital from an outer fief as a capital official; old Eastern Capital officials mostly looked down on him; as for deploying military affairs, they did not much defer to his orders.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zigai had only lately come from a provincial post to serve in the capital, and many longtime Eastern Capital officials slighted him; they did not readily accept his orders when it came to military dispositions.

sentences.zh: 裴弘策與子蓋同班，前出討賊失利，子蓋更使出戰，不肯行，子蓋命引出斬之以徇。

translations.literal: Pei Hongce and Zigai were of equal rank; having earlier gone out to attack the rebels and lost, Zigai ordered him out again to fight; he refused to go, and Zigai ordered him led out and beheaded as example.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Hongce held the same rank as Zigai; after his earlier defeat against the rebels, Zigai ordered him out again—Hongce refused, and Zigai had him executed before the troops as a warning.

sentences.zh: 國子祭酒河東楊汪，小有不恭，子蓋又將斬之；

translations.literal: Director of the National University Yang Wang of Hedong showed slight disrespect; Zigai was about to behead him again;
translations.idiomatic: When Director of the National University Yang Wang of Hedong showed even slight disrespect, Zigai again meant to execute him;

sentences.zh: 汪頓首流血，乃得免。

translations.literal: Wang kowtowed until blood flowed, and only then was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Wang kowtowed until his brow bled, and was spared.

sentences.zh: 於是將吏震肅，無敢仰視，令行禁止。

translations.literal: Thereupon officers and clerks were awed into discipline; none dared look up; orders went forth and prohibitions were enforced.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the officers stood in terrified obedience, none daring even to meet his gaze—his orders were obeyed without question.

sentences.zh: 玄感盡銳攻城，子蓋隨方拒守，玄感不能克。

translations.literal: Xuangan mustered all elite troops to assault the city; Zigai defended wherever attacked; Xuangan could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan threw his best troops against the walls, and Zigai met him at every point; Xuangan could not break through.

sentences.zh: 然達官子弟應募從軍者，聞弘策死，皆不敢入城。

translations.literal: Yet sons of high officials who had joined the army on enlistment, hearing of Hongce's death, all dared not enter the city.
translations.idiomatic: Still, sons of high officials who had enlisted dared not enter the city after Hongce's execution.

sentences.zh: 韓擒虎子世咢、觀王雄子恭道、虞世基子柔、來護兒子淵、裴蘊子爽、大理卿鄭善果子儼、周羅睺子仲等四十餘人皆降於玄感，玄感悉以親要重任委之。

translations.literal: Han Qihu's son Shi'e, Prince of Guan Xiong's son Gongdao, Yu Shiji's son Rou, Lai Huer's son Yuan, Pei Zi's son Shuang, Grand Judge of Justice Zheng Shanguo's son Yan, Zhou Luohou's son Zhong, and more than forty others all surrendered to Xuangan; Xuangan entrusted them all with intimate, important duties.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qihu's son Shi'e, Prince of Guan Yang Xiong's son Gongdao, Yu Shiji's son Rou, Lai Huer's son Yuan, Pei Zi's son Shuang, Chief Minister of Justice Zheng Shanguo's son Yan, Zhou Luohou's son Zhong, and more than forty others all defected to Xuangan, who put them in positions of trust and authority.

sentences.zh: 善果，譯之兄子也。

translations.literal: Shanguo was nephew of the elder Yizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Shanguo was a nephew of Yizhi.

sentences.zh: 玄感收兵得五萬餘人，發五千守慈澗道，五千守伊闕道，遣韓世咢將三千人圍滎陽，顧覺將五千人取虎牢。

translations.literal: Xuangan gathered troops totaling more than fifty thousand, sent five thousand to guard Cijian Road, five thousand to guard Yique Road, dispatched Han Shi'e with three thousand to besiege Xingyang, and Gu Jue with five thousand to take Hulao.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan's ranks swelled to more than fifty thousand; he posted five thousand to hold Cijian Pass and five thousand Yique Pass, sent Han Shi'e with three thousand to besiege Xingyang, and Gu Jue with five thousand to take Hulao.

sentences.zh: 虎牢降，以覺為鄭州刺史，鎮虎牢。

translations.literal: Hulao surrendered; he made Jue Prefect of Zhengzhou and garrisoned Hulao.
translations.idiomatic: When Hulao surrendered, he appointed Jue Prefect of Zhengzhou and left him to guard the fortress.

sentences.zh: 代王侑使刑部尚書衛文升帥兵四萬救東都，文升至華陰，掘楊素塚，焚其骸骨，示士卒以必死，遂鼓行出崤、澠，直趨東都城北。

translations.literal: Prince of Dai Yang You sent Minister of Justice Wei Wensheng to command forty thousand troops to relieve the Eastern Capital; Wensheng reached Huayin, dug up Yang Su's tomb, burned his bones, showed the troops he would fight to the death, then marched with drums out through Xiao and Mian, straight toward the north of the Eastern Capital city.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Dai Yang You sent Minister of Justice Wei Wensheng with forty thousand men to relieve the Eastern Capital; at Huayin Wensheng opened Yang Su's tomb and burned the bones, showing his men he would fight to the death, then marched with drums sounding through the Xiao and Mian passes straight for the north wall of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 玄感逆拒之；

translations.literal: Xuangan went out to oppose him;
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan marched out to block him;

sentences.zh: 文升且戰且行，屯於金谷。

translations.literal: Wensheng fought as he went and encamped at Golden Valley.
translations.idiomatic: Wensheng fought as he advanced and encamped at Jingu.

sentences.zh: 遼東城久不拔，帝遣造布囊百餘萬口，滿貯土，欲積為魚梁大道，闊三十步，高與城齊，使戰士登而攻之。

translations.literal: The Liaodong city long un taken, the emperor ordered cloth bags made numbering more than a million mouths, filled with earth, intending to pile them into a fish-bridge roadway thirty paces wide, as high as the city, for warriors to climb and attack.
translations.idiomatic: As the siege of Liaodong dragged on, the emperor ordered more than a million cloth sacks filled with earth to build a raised assault ramp thirty paces wide and level with the walls, so his soldiers could climb it to attack.

sentences.zh: 又作八輪樓車，高出於城，夾魚梁道，欲俯射城內，指期將攻，城內危蹙。

translations.literal: He also made eight-wheeled tower carts higher than the city, flanking the fish-bridge road, intending to shoot down into the city; the attack was set for a fixed day; inside the city was perilously pressed.
translations.idiomatic: He also built eight-wheeled siege towers taller than the walls, lining the ramp, to rain missiles down on the defenders; with the assault set for a fixed day, the city was in desperate straits.

sentences.zh: 會楊玄感反書至，帝大懼，引納言蘇威入帳中，謂曰：「此兒聰明，得無為患？」

translations.literal: When Yang Xuangan's rebel letter arrived, the emperor was greatly afraid; he led Remonstrating Censor Su Wei into the tent and said: "This son is clever—will he not become a trouble?"
translations.idiomatic: When word of Yang Xuangan's revolt arrived, the emperor was deeply alarmed; he drew Remonstrating Censor Su Wei into his tent and said: "That boy is clever—won't he become a serious threat?"

sentences.zh: 威曰：「夫識是非，審成敗，乃謂之聰明，玄感粗疏，必無所慮。

translations.literal: Wei said: "To know right from wrong and judge success and failure—that is called cleverness; Xuangan is coarse and careless, surely without such forethought.
translations.idiomatic: Wei said: "True cleverness means knowing right from wrong and weighing success and failure—Xuangan is rash and shallow and surely lacks that.

sentences.zh: 但恐因此浸成亂階耳。」

translations.literal: But I fear that from this will gradually arise the steps of disorder."
translations.idiomatic: I only fear this may slowly open the door to wider rebellion."

sentences.zh: 帝又聞達官子弟皆在玄感所，益憂之。

translations.literal: The emperor also heard that sons of high officials were all with Xuangan and grew more worried.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also learned that sons of the great families had joined Xuangan, and his anxiety grew.

sentences.zh: 兵部侍郎斛斯政素與玄感善，玄感之反，政與之通謀，玄縱兄弟亡歸，政潛遣之。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of War Qisi Zheng had long been friendly with Xuangan; when Xuangan rebelled, Zheng conspired with him—the Xuanzong brothers fled home, and Zheng secretly sent them off.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of War Qisi Zheng had long been close to Xuangan; when the rebellion broke out Zheng colluded with him, and when the Xuanzong brothers fled home Zheng secretly helped them escape.

sentences.zh: 帝將窮治玄縱等黨與，政內不自安，戊辰，亡奔高麗。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to pursue and punish the Xuanzong clique; Zheng was inwardly unsettled; on wuchen he fled to Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor prepared to root out the Xuanzong faction, Zheng lost his nerve; on wuchen he fled to Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 庚午，夜二更，帝密召諸將，使引軍還，軍資、器械、攻具，積如丘山，營壘、帳幕、案堵不動，皆棄之而去。

translations.literal: On gengwu, at the second watch of night, the emperor secretly summoned the generals and had them lead the army back; military supplies, weapons, and siege equipment piled like hills; encampments, tents, and walls stood unmoved—all abandoned and left.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, at the second watch of night, the emperor secretly summoned his generals and ordered a withdrawal; supplies, arms, and siege gear lay heaped like hills, and camps, tents, and palisades stood untouched—all abandoned as they marched away.

sentences.zh: 眾心忷懼，無復部分，諸道分散。

translations.literal: The host's hearts were alarmed and fearful; there was no longer order; the various routes scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Panic spread through the ranks; units lost all cohesion and broke up along separate routes.

sentences.zh: 高麗即時覺之，然不敢出，但於城內鼓噪。

translations.literal: Goguryeo immediately noticed, yet dared not come out, only beating drums and shouting within the city.
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo noticed at once, but dared not sally out—they only beat drums and shout within the walls.

sentences.zh: 至來日午時，方漸出外，四遠覘偵，猶疑隋軍詐之。

translations.literal: By noon the next day they gradually ventured out; spies from far around still suspected the Sui army was feigning.
translations.idiomatic: Not until noon the next day did they gradually emerge; scouts from all quarters still suspected a Sui trick.

sentences.zh: 經二日，乃出數千兵追躡，畏隋軍之眾，不敢逼，常相去八九十里，將至遼水，知御營畢渡，乃敢逼後軍。

translations.literal: After two days they sent out several thousand troops to pursue; fearing the Sui host's numbers, they dared not press close, always keeping eight or ninety li apart; nearing the Liao River, learning the imperial camp had all crossed, only then dared press the rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: After two days they sent out several thousand men in pursuit; fearing Sui numbers, they kept eighty or ninety li back; only when they neared the Liao River and saw the imperial camp fully across did they dare close on the rear guard.

sentences.zh: 時後軍猶數萬人，高麗隨而抄擊，最後羸弱數千人為所殺略。

translations.literal: At that time the rear guard still numbered tens of thousands; Goguryeo followed and raided; the last weak few thousand were killed and plundered by them.
translations.idiomatic: The rear guard still numbered in the tens of thousands, but Goguryeo harried them from behind; the weakest few thousand at the tail were killed and stripped.

sentences.zh: 初，帝再征高麗，復問太史令庚質曰：「今段何如？」

translations.literal: Earlier, when the emperor again campaigned against Goguryeo, he again asked Grand Astrologer Geng Zhi: "How is this expedition?"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the emperor set out on his second Goguryeo campaign, he again asked Grand Astrologer Geng Zhi: "What do you make of this expedition?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣實愚迷，猶執前見，陛下若親動萬乘，勞費實多。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Your servant is truly dull and confused, yet still holds my earlier view—if Your Majesty personally moves the imperial carriage, labor and expense will truly be great."
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "I am a dull man, but I still hold to my earlier view—if Your Majesty leads the host in person, the cost in labor and treasure will be enormous."

sentences.zh: 帝怒曰：「我自行猶不克，直遣人去，安得有功！」

translations.literal: The emperor angrily said: "If I go myself it still may not succeed—simply send others, how can there be achievement!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor snapped: "If I go and still fail, how could sending someone else succeed!"

sentences.zh: 及還，謂質曰：「卿前不欲我行，當為此耳。

translations.literal: When he returned, he said to Zhi: "You before did not want me to go—it was for this.
translations.idiomatic: After his return he said to Geng Zhi: "You did not want me to go—it was because of this.

sentences.zh: 玄感其有成乎？」

translations.literal: Will Xuangan succeed?"
translations.idiomatic: Will Xuangan succeed?"

sentences.zh: 質曰：「玄感地勢雖隆，素非人望，因百姓之勞，冀幸成功。

translations.literal: Zhi said: "Though Xuangan's terrain position is elevated, he has never been men's hope; relying on the people's exhaustion, he hopes by luck to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Zhi said: "Though Xuangan holds strong ground, he has never commanded popular respect; he is betting on the people's exhaustion and hoping for a lucky break.

sentences.zh: 今天下一家，未易可動。」

translations.literal: Now the realm is one family; not easy to stir."
translations.idiomatic: The realm is still one house—not easily moved."

sentences.zh: 帝遣虎賁郎將陳稜攻元務本於黎陽，又遣左翊衛大將軍宇文述、左候衛將軍屈突通乘傳發兵以討玄感。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Tiger Guard Commandant Chen Ling to attack Wu Ben at Liyang, and also sent Left Wing Guard Grand General Yuwen Shu and Left Garrison Guard General Qutu Tong by post relays to dispatch troops against Xuangan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Tiger Guard Commandant Chen Ling to attack Wu Ben at Liyang, and dispatched Left Wing Guard Grand General Yuwen Shu and Left Garrison Guard General Qutu Tong by fast relay to raise troops against Xuangan.

sentences.zh: 來護兒至東萊，聞玄感圍東都，召諸將議旋軍救之。

translations.literal: Lai Huer reached Donglai, heard Xuangan besieged the Eastern Capital, summoned the generals to discuss turning the army to rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: When Lai Huer reached Donglai and learned Xuangan was besieging the Eastern Capital, he called his generals to discuss marching back to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 諸將咸以無敕，不宜擅還，固執不從，護兒厲聲曰：「洛陽被圍，心腹之疾；

translations.literal: The generals all said there was no edict and they should not return on their own; stubbornly they would not obey; Huer said sternly: "Luoyang besieged is a disease of heart and belly;
translations.idiomatic: The generals argued that without an imperial order they must not withdraw on their own and stubbornly refused; Huer declared in a stern voice: "Luoyang under siege is a wound to the heart;

sentences.zh: 高麗逆命，猶疥癬耳。

translations.literal: Goguryeo's defiance is but scabies and tinea.
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo's rebellion is nothing but a skin rash.

sentences.zh: 公家之事，知無不為，專擅在吾，不關諸人，有沮議者，軍法從事！」

translations.literal: In the state's affairs, knowing something one does not act on—sole authority is mine, not the others' concern; whoever obstructs with words, military law will deal with!"
translations.idiomatic: In the emperor's service one acts when action is needed—the decision is mine alone and none of yours; whoever argues against it, let military law deal with him!"

sentences.zh: 即日回軍。

translations.literal: That same day he turned the army back.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he turned the army about.

sentences.zh: 令子弘、整馳驛奏聞。

translations.literal: He ordered his sons Hong and Zheng to gallop by post relay to report.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his sons Hong and Zheng by express relay to inform the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝時還至涿郡，已敕護兒救東都，見弘、整，甚悅，賜護兒璽書曰：「公旋師之時，是朕敕公之日，君臣意合，遠同符契。」

translations.literal: The emperor at the time had returned to Zhuo Commandery and had already edicted Huer to save the Eastern Capital; seeing Hong and Zheng, he was very pleased, and bestowed on Huer an imperial letter saying: "The day you turned the army was the day I edicted you; lord and minister in accord, distant yet as one tally."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then returning to Zhuo Commandery and had already ordered Huer to relieve the Eastern Capital; when he saw Hong and Zheng he was delighted and sent Huer an imperial letter saying: "The day you turned your army was the day I commanded you to do so—monarch and minister thinking as one, though far apart, as if sealed by one tally."

sentences.zh: 先是，右武候大將軍李子雄坐事除名，令從軍自效，從來護兒在東萊，帝疑之，詔鎖子雄至行在所。

translations.literal: Earlier, Right Martial Inspector Grand General Li Zixiong was dismissed from office for a crime, ordered to join the army to redeem himself, followed Lai Huer at Donglai; the emperor suspected him and edicted him shackled to the traveling court.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Right Martial Inspector Grand General Li Zixiong had been stripped of rank for an offense and ordered to redeem himself in the field under Lai Huer at Donglai; the emperor grew suspicious and ordered him chained and brought to the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 子雄殺使者，逃奔玄感。

translations.literal: Zixiong killed the envoy and fled to Xuangan.
translations.idiomatic: Zixiong killed the messenger and fled to join Xuangan.

sentences.zh: 衛文升以步騎二萬渡瀍水，與玄感戰，玄感屢破之。

translations.literal: Wei Wensheng with twenty thousand foot and horse crossed the Chan River, fought Xuangan, and Xuangan repeatedly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Wensheng crossed the Chan River with twenty thousand infantry and cavalry and fought Xuangan, who routed him again and again.

sentences.zh: 玄感每戰，身先士卒，所向摧陷，又善撫悅其下，皆樂為致死，由是每戰多捷，眾益盛，至十萬人。

translations.literal: Each battle Xuangan led from the front; wherever he went he broke through; he also knew how to comfort and please his men, all gladly dying for him; thus each battle mostly succeeded, his host ever swelled, reaching one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan always fought at the head of his men and broke through wherever he led; he also knew how to win his troops' hearts, and they gladly fought to the death for him—battle after battle he won, and his ranks swelled to a hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 文升眾寡不敵，死傷太半且盡，乃更進屯邙山之陽，與玄感決戰，一日十餘合。

translations.literal: Wensheng, outnumbered, with dead and wounded more than half and nearly gone, again advanced and encamped on the sunny south of Mount Mang, fought decisive battle with Xuangan—more than ten clashes in one day.
translations.idiomatic: Outnumbered and with more than half his force killed or wounded, Wensheng pressed on to the south slope of Mount Mang and fought a decisive battle with Xuangan—more than ten engagements in a single day.

sentences.zh: 會楊玄挺中流矢死，玄感軍乃稍卻。

translations.literal: When Yang Xuanting was struck by a flowing arrow and died, Xuangan's army then slightly retreated.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xuanting took an arrow and died, Xuangan's army began to give ground.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，癸未，餘杭民劉元進起兵以應玄感。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, guiwei—Liu Yuanjin of Yuhang raised troops to respond to Xuangan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on guiwei, Liu Yuanjin of Yuhang took up arms in support of Xuangan.

sentences.zh: 元進手長尺餘，臂垂過膝，自以相表非常，陰有異志。

translations.literal: Yuanjin's hands were more than a chi long, arms hanging past knees; he considered his physique extraordinary and secretly harbored different ambitions.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjin's hands measured more than a foot, his arms hung below his knees; he took his unusual build as a sign of destiny and secretly nursed ambitions of his own.

sentences.zh: 會帝再發三吳征高麗，三吳兵皆相謂曰：「往歲天下全盛，吾輩父兄征高麗者猶太半不返；

translations.literal: When the emperor again mobilized the Three Wu for Goguryeo, the Three Wu soldiers all said to one another: "In past years when the realm was fully prosperous, our fathers and brothers who campaigned against Goguryeo—more than half did not return;
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor again conscripted the Three Wu for Goguryeo, the soldiers there said among themselves: "In years past when the empire was at its height, more than half of our fathers and brothers sent against Goguryeo never came back;

sentences.zh: 今已罷弊，復為此行，吾屬無遺類矣！」

translations.literal: Now already exhausted, again made for this expedition—our sort will leave no survivors!"
translations.idiomatic: and now, worn to the bone, we are sent again on the same errand—not one of us will survive!"

sentences.zh: 由是多亡命。

translations.literal: From this many became fugitives.
translations.idiomatic: Many took to flight as outlaws.

sentences.zh: 郡縣捕之急，聞元進舉兵，亡命者雲集，旬月間，眾至數萬。

translations.literal: When prefectures and counties pursued them urgently, hearing Yuanjin raised troops, fugitives gathered like clouds; within a month or so, the host reached tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: As counties hunted them down, fugitives streamed to Yuanjin when he raised his banner; within a month his following swelled to tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 始，楊玄感至東都，自謂天下響應，功在朝夕。

translations.literal: At first, when Yang Xuangan reached the Eastern Capital, he considered that the realm would respond, success within days.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuangan first reached the Eastern Capital, he expected the realm to rally to him and victory within days.

sentences.zh: 得韋福嗣，委以心膂，不復專任李密。

translations.literal: Having obtained Wei Fusi, he entrusted him as heart and spine, no longer relying solely on Li Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had Wei Fusi, he treated him as his right hand and no longer relied on Li Mi alone.

sentences.zh: 福嗣每畫策，皆持兩端；

translations.literal: Each time Fusi plotted strategy, he held both ends;
translations.idiomatic: Fusi's every plan hedged both ways;

sentences.zh: 密揣知其意，謂玄感曰：「福嗣元非同盟，實懷觀望；

translations.literal: Mi guessed his intent and said to Xuangan: "Fusi was never truly allied; in truth he harbors watchful waiting;
translations.idiomatic: Mi saw through him and told Xuangan: "Fusi was never truly one of us—he is watching to see which way the wind blows;

sentences.zh: 明公初起大事而奸人在側，聽其是非，必為所誤，請斬之！」

translations.literal: My lord, beginning a great undertaking with a traitor at your side, listening to his right and wrong—you will surely be misled by him; please behead him!"
translations.idiomatic: you have begun a great enterprise with a traitor at your side; if you heed his advice you will surely be ruined—I beg you, execute him!"

sentences.zh: 玄感曰：「何至於此！」

translations.literal: Xuangan said: "How can it come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan said: "Surely it need not go that far!"

sentences.zh: 密退，謂所親曰：「楚公好反而不欲勝，吾屬今為虜矣！」

translations.literal: Mi withdrew and said to intimates: "Lord Chu loves turning back and does not wish to win—we are captives now!"
translations.idiomatic: Mi withdrew and told his confidants: "Lord Chu loves rebellion but not victory—we are prisoners already!"

sentences.zh: 李子雄勸玄感速稱尊號，玄感以問密，密曰：「昔陳勝自欲稱王，張耳諫而被外；

translations.literal: Li Zixiong urged Xuangan quickly to assume imperial title; Xuangan asked Mi; Mi said: "Formerly Chen Sheng himself wished to call himself king; Zhang Er remonstrated and was cast out;
translations.idiomatic: Li Zixiong urged Xuangan to proclaim himself emperor at once; Xuangan asked Mi, who said: "When Chen Sheng wanted to make himself king, Zhang Er cautioned him and was cast out;

sentences.zh: 魏武將求九錫，荀彧止而見誅。

translations.literal: Wei Wu was about to seek the Nine Bestowals; Xun Yu stopped him and was put to death.
translations.idiomatic: when Cao Cao sought the Nine Bestowals, Xun Yu opposed him and was killed.

sentences.zh: 今者密欲正言，還恐追蹤二子；

translations.literal: Now if Mi wishes to speak uprightly, he still fears following in the footsteps of those two;
translations.idiomatic: If I speak plainly now, I fear I will share the fate of those two;

sentences.zh: 阿諛順意，又非密之本圖。

translations.literal: Flattering and agreeing with one's wishes is again not Mi's original intent.
translations.idiomatic: yet to flatter and agree with you would betray everything I stand for.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: How so?
translations.idiomatic: Why is that?

sentences.zh: 兵起以來，雖復頻捷，至於郡縣，未有從者；

translations.literal: Since the army rose, though victories have been frequent, as for commanderies and counties, none have joined;
translations.idiomatic: Since we took up arms, we have won battle after battle, yet no commandery or county has rallied to our cause;

sentences.zh: 東都守禦尚強，天下救兵益至，公當挺身力戰，早定關中，乃亟欲自尊，何示人不廣也！」

translations.literal: The Eastern Capital's defense is still strong; relief armies from all under Heaven arrive ever more—you, sir, ought to throw yourself bodily into fierce battle and quickly settle Guanzhong, yet you urgently wish to exalt yourself—what lack of breadth do you show to men!"
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Capital still holds strong, and relief armies from across the empire arrive daily—you should throw yourself into the fight and secure Guanzhong first, yet you rush to proclaim yourself ruler. What a cramped signal to send the world!"

sentences.zh: 玄感笑而止。

translations.literal: Xuangan laughed and desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan laughed and said no more.

sentences.zh: 屈突通引兵屯河陽，宇文述繼之，玄感問計於李子雄，子雄曰：「通曉習兵事，若一得渡河，則勝負難決，不如分兵拒之。

translations.literal: Qu Tutong led troops to encamp at Heyang; Yuwen Shu followed; Xuangan asked Li Zixiong for advice; Zixiong said: "Tong is well versed in military matters; if he once crosses the river, victory and defeat will be hard to decide—better to divide troops to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Tutong encamped his army at Heyang, with Yuwen Shu coming up behind him. Xuangan consulted Li Zixiong, who said: "Tutong knows his craft. Once he crosses the river, the outcome becomes uncertain—we should detach a force to block him.

sentences.zh: 通不能濟，則樊、衛失援。」

translations.literal: If Tong cannot cross, then Fan and Wei lose support."
translations.idiomatic: If he cannot get across, Fan and Wei will be cut off from help."

sentences.zh: 玄感然之，將拒通；

translations.literal: Xuangan approved; he would resist Tong;
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan agreed and prepared to block Tutong;

sentences.zh: 樊子蓋知其謀，數擊其營，玄感不得往。

translations.literal: Fan Zigai knew his plan and repeatedly attacked his camp; Xuangan could not go.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zigai learned of the plan and struck his camps again and again, so Xuangan never got there.

sentences.zh: 通濟河，軍於破陵。

translations.literal: Tong crossed the river and encamped at Poling.
translations.idiomatic: Tutong crossed the river and made camp at Poling.

sentences.zh: 玄感分為二軍，西抗文升，東拒通。

translations.literal: Xuangan divided into two armies—west to resist Wensheng, east to resist Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan split his forces: one wing to hold off Wei Wensheng in the west, the other to face Tutong in the east.

sentences.zh: 子蓋復出兵大戰，玄感軍屢敗，與其黨謀之，李子雄曰：「東都援軍益至，我軍數敗，不可久留，不如直入關中，開永豐倉以振貧乏，三輔可指麾而定，據有府庫，東面而爭天下，亦霸王之業也。」

translations.literal: Zigai again sent troops for a great battle; Xuangan's army was repeatedly defeated; with his partisans he deliberated; Li Zixiong said: "Eastern Capital relief armies arrive ever more; our army has been defeated several times—we cannot linger long; better to enter Guanzhong directly, open Yongfeng Granary to aid the poor and destitute; the Three Adjuncts can be settled at a gesture; holding the treasury stores, facing east to contend for All under Heaven—this too is an hegemon-king's enterprise."
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zigai launched another major assault, and Xuangan's troops lost again and again. In council with his followers, Li Zixiong said: "Relief for the Eastern Capital grows daily, and we keep losing—we cannot stay here. Better to strike straight into Guanzhong, open the Yongfeng Granary to feed the hungry, and sweep the Three Adjuncts at a wave of the hand. With the imperial storehouses in our grip, we can turn east and contest the realm—that is the path of a true hegemon."

sentences.zh: 李密曰：「弘化留守元弘嗣握強兵在隴右，可聲言其反，遣使迎公，因此入關，可以紿眾。」

translations.literal: Li Mi said: "Honghua garrison commander Yuan Hongsi holds strong troops in Longyou; one may proclaim that he has rebelled, send envoys to welcome you, sir, and by this enter the Pass—thus one can deceive the multitude."
translations.idiomatic: Mi said: "Yuan Hongsi, the garrison commander at Honghua, commands a strong force in Longyou. Declare that he has risen in rebellion and send envoys to welcome you—use that pretext to enter the passes and keep the army believing."

sentences.zh: 會華陰諸楊請為嚮導，壬辰，玄感解東都圍，引兵西趣潼關，宣言：「我已破東都，取關西矣！」

translations.literal: Just then the various Yangs of Huayin requested to serve as guides; on renchen, Xuangan lifted the siege of the Eastern Capital, led troops west toward Tong Pass, and proclaimed: "I have already broken the Eastern Capital and taken the land west of the Pass!"
translations.idiomatic: The Yang clan of Huayin offered to guide them. On renchen day, Xuangan raised the siege of the Eastern Capital and marched west toward Tong Pass, declaring: "I have taken the Eastern Capital—Guanzhong is mine!"

sentences.zh: 宇文述等諸軍躡之。

translations.literal: The various armies of Yuwen Shu and others pursued him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Shu and the other imperial armies pressed in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 至弘農宮，父老遮說玄感曰：「宮城空虛，又多積粟，攻之易下。」

translations.literal: Reaching Hongnong Palace, elders blocked the way and urged Xuangan: "The palace city is empty and also holds much stored grain—attacking it, it is easy to take."
translations.idiomatic: At Hongnong Palace, local elders waylaid Xuangan and said: "The palace stands nearly empty yet is packed with grain—it would fall easily to assault."

sentences.zh: 玄感以為然。

translations.literal: Xuangan thought it so.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan agreed.

sentences.zh: 弘農太守蔡王智積謂官屬曰：「玄感聞大軍將至，欲西圖關中，若成其計，則難克也；

translations.literal: Hongnong prefect Cai Wang Zhiji said to subordinates: "Xuangan, hearing the great army is about to arrive, wishes to plot west for Guanzhong; if his plan succeeds, he will be hard to overcome;
translations.idiomatic: Hongnong's prefect, Prince of Cai Zhiji, told his staff: "Xuangan means to break through into Guanzhong before the main army arrives. If he succeeds, he will be impossible to crush;

sentences.zh: 當以計縻之，使不得進，不出一旬，可以成擒。」

translations.literal: one ought with a stratagem to tether him, so he cannot advance; within ten days, he can be captured complete."
translations.idiomatic: we must use a stratagem to tie him down and keep him from advancing—in less than ten days we can take him alive."

sentences.zh: 及玄感軍至城下，智積登陴詈之；

translations.literal: When Xuangan's army reached below the walls, Zhiji ascended the ramparts and reviled him;
translations.idiomatic: When Xuangan's army reached the walls, Zhiji climbed the battlements and hurled insults at him;

sentences.zh: 玄感怒，留攻之。

translations.literal: Xuangan grew angry and stayed to attack it.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Xuangan halted to lay siege.

sentences.zh: 李密諫曰：「公今詐眾西入，軍事貴速，況乃追兵將至，安可稽留！

translations.literal: Li Mi remonstrated: "You, sir, now deceive the multitude by entering west; in warfare speed is prized—moreover pursuing troops are about to arrive—how can one linger!
translations.idiomatic: Mi urged him: "You have deceived the army into marching west—war demands speed, and the pursuers are close. How can we delay here!

sentences.zh: 若前不得據關，退無所守，大眾一散，何以自全！」

translations.literal: If forward one cannot hold the Pass, retreat having nowhere to defend, the great host once scattered—how preserve oneself!"
translations.idiomatic: If we fail to seize the passes ahead, we will have nowhere to fall back—and once this host disperses, none of us survives!"

sentences.zh: 玄感不從，遂攻之，燒其城門，智積於內益火，玄感兵不得入。

translations.literal: Xuangan did not follow; then attacked; burned its gate; Zhiji inside increased fire; Xuangan's troops could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan refused to listen. He pressed the assault and set fire to the gate, but Zhiji kindled flames inside as well, and Xuangan's men could not break through.

sentences.zh: 三日不拔，乃引而西。

translations.literal: Three days without taking it, then led away westward.
translations.idiomatic: After three days without success, he marched on toward the west.

sentences.zh: 至閺鄉，宇文述、衛文昇、來護兒、屈突通等軍追及於皇天原。

translations.literal: Reaching Wenxiang, the armies of Yuwen Shu, Wei Wensheng, Lai Huer, Qu Tutong, and others caught up at Huangtian Plain.
translations.idiomatic: At Wenxiang, the armies of Yuwen Shu, Wei Wensheng, Lai Huer, and Qu Tutong caught up with him on Huangtian Plain.

sentences.zh: 玄感上槃豆，布陳亙五十里，且戰且行，玄感一日三敗。

translations.literal: Xuangan ascended Panyu, deployed battle lines spanning fifty li, fighting as he marched; Xuangan in one day was thrice defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan took up positions at Mount Pandou, drawing his battle line along fifty li of road as he fought and retreated—and suffered three defeats in a single day.

sentences.zh: 八月，壬寅，玄感陳於董杜原，諸軍擊之，玄感大敗，獨與十餘騎奔上洛。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on renyin, Xuangan formed battle at Dongdu Plain; the various armies struck; Xuangan was greatly defeated; alone with a dozen-odd riders he fled toward Shangluo.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on renyin day, Xuangan made his stand on Dongdu Plain. The imperial armies struck and shattered him. With barely a dozen riders he fled toward Shangluo.

sentences.zh: 追騎至，玄感叱之，皆反走。

translations.literal: Pursuing horsemen arrived; Xuangan shouted at them; all turned and fled back.
translations.idiomatic: When pursuers caught up, Xuangan roared at them and they wheeled about in flight.

sentences.zh: 至葭蘆戍，獨與弟積善徒步走，自度不免，謂積善曰：「我不能受人戮辱，汝可殺我！」

translations.literal: Reaching Jialu Post, alone with younger brother Jishan fleeing on foot; judging he could not escape, he said to Jishan: "I cannot bear to suffer slaughter and humiliation at others' hands—you may kill me!"
translations.idiomatic: At Jialu Post he fled on foot with only his brother Jishan. Seeing capture was inevitable, he told Jishan: "I will not endure the humiliation of execution—kill me yourself!"

sentences.zh: 積善抽刀斫殺之，因自刺，不死，為追兵所執，與玄感首俱送行在所。

translations.literal: Jishan drew sword and hacked him to death; then stabbed himself; did not die; was seized by pursuing troops; together with Xuangan's head all were sent to the emperor's traveling encampment.
translations.idiomatic: Jishan drew his blade and struck him down, then tried to take his own life but failed. Pursuers seized him and sent him, with Xuangan's severed head, to the emperor's camp.

sentences.zh: 磔玄感屍於東都市，三日，復臠而焚之。

translations.literal: Xuangan's corpse was dismembered and displayed in the Eastern Capital market; after three days, again sliced and burned.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan's body was dismembered and displayed in the Eastern Capital market. After three days it was cut to pieces and burned.

sentences.zh: 玄感弟玄獎為義陽太守，將赴玄感，為郡丞周旋玉所殺；
