translations.literal: Xuangan's younger brother Xuanjiang was Yiyang prefect; about to go join Xuangan; was killed by assistant prefect Zhou Xuanyu;
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan's brother Xuanjiang, prefect of Yiyang, was marching to join the rebellion when the assistant prefect Zhou Xuanyu killed him;

sentences.zh: 仁行為朝請大夫，伏誅於長安。

translations.literal: Renxing was a Palace Attendant; was executed at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Renxing, a court gentleman, was put to death in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 玄感之圍東都也，梁郡民韓相國舉兵應之，玄感以為河南道元帥，旬月間眾十餘萬，攻剽郡縣；

translations.literal: When Xuangan besieged the Eastern Capital, Liang commandery commoner Han Xiangguo raised troops in response; Xuangan made him Henan Circuit marshal; within ten days and a month his host was a hundred thousand-plus, attacking and plundering commanderies and counties;
translations.idiomatic: While Xuangan besieged the Eastern Capital, Han Xiangguo of Liang commandery rose in support. Xuangan appointed him commander of the Henan circuit, and within a month his following swelled to more than a hundred thousand as they raided commanderies and counties.

sentences.zh: 至襄城，聞玄感敗，眾稍散，為吏所獲，傳首東都。

translations.literal: Reaching Xiangcheng, hearing Xuangan defeated, the host gradually dispersed; was seized by officials; head sent to Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiangcheng he learned of Xuangan's defeat; his army melted away, and officials captured him and sent his head to the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 帝以元弘嗣，斛斯政之親也，留守弘化郡，遣衛尉少卿李淵馳往執之，因代為留守，關右十三郡兵皆受徵發。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Yuan Hongsi was a kinsman of Qisi Zheng, garrisoned at Honghua commandery—sent Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Li Yuan galloping to seize him, and replaced him as garrison commander; the troops of the thirteen commanderies west of the Pass all received mobilization.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yuan Hongsi was a relative of Qisi Zheng, the emperor had stationed him at Honghua. He dispatched Li Yuan, vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, to arrest him and take over the garrison. All thirteen commanderies of Longyou were mobilized.

sentences.zh: 淵御眾寬簡，人多附之。

translations.literal: Yuan governed the masses with lenient simplicity; many men attached to him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan ruled with a light hand, and people flocked to him.

sentences.zh: 帝以淵相表奇異，又名應圖讖，忌之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Yuan's physiognomy was extraordinary, and his name matched prognostic charts—feared him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor noted Li Yuan's unusual features and a name that matched prophetic texts—and grew wary of him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，徵詣行在所，淵遇疾未謁，其甥王氏在後宮，帝問曰：「汝舅來何遲？」

translations.literal: Before long, summoned to the traveling encampment; Yuan fell ill and had not yet had audience; his nephew's daughter the Lady Wang was in the inner palace; the emperor asked: "Why is your uncle's coming so late?"
translations.idiomatic: Soon Li Yuan was summoned to the emperor's camp, but illness delayed his audience. His niece Lady Wang served in the inner palace, and the emperor asked her: "Why is your uncle so slow to appear?"

sentences.zh: 王氏以疾對，帝曰：「可得死否？」

translations.literal: Lady Wang answered with illness; the emperor said: "Can he obtain death?"
translations.idiomatic: She cited his illness. The emperor said: "Might he die, perhaps?"

sentences.zh: 淵聞之，懼，因縱酒納賂以自晦。

translations.literal: Yuan heard it; feared; therefore indulged in wine and accepted bribes to obscure himself.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan heard of this and was terrified. He took to drunkenness and bribery to make himself seem harmless.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，吳郡朱燮、晉陵管崇聚眾寇掠江左。

translations.literal: On guimao, Wu commandery's Zhu Xie and Jinling's Guan Chong gathered masses to raid and plunder the left of the Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao day, Zhu Xie of Wu commandery and Guan Chong of Jinling raised bands to pillage the lands south of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 燮本還俗道人，涉獵經史，頗知兵法，形容眇小，為昆山縣博士，與數十學生起兵，民苦役者赴之如歸。

translations.literal: Xie was originally a returned-to-lay-life Taoist priest; broadly read classics and histories; quite knew military arts; stature small and slight; was Kunshan county Erudite; with several tens of students raised troops; people suffering corvée labor went to him as homeward.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xie had been a defrocked Taoist priest, well read in the classics and versed in military strategy, though slight of build. A county erudite in Kunshan, he took up arms with a few dozen students, and labor-weary commoners rallied to him as though returning home.

sentences.zh: 崇長大，美姿容，志氣倜儻，隱居常熟，自言有王者相，故群盜相與奉之。

translations.literal: Chong was tall and large; handsome in bearing; spirit lofty and unrestrained; lived in seclusion at Changshu; himself said he had the physiognomy of a king—therefore bandits together honored him.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Chong was tall and handsome, bold and free-spirited, living in seclusion at Changshu. He claimed the bearing of a king, and the bandits made him their leader.

sentences.zh: 時帝在涿郡，命虎牙郎將趙六兒將兵萬人屯楊子，分為五營以備南賊。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor was at Zhuo commandery; ordered Tiger Fang General Zhao Liu'er to lead ten thousand troops to encamp at Yangzi, divided into five camps to guard against southern bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then at Zhuo commandery. He ordered General Zhao Liu'er of the Tiger Guards to encamp ten thousand men at Yangzi in five camps against the southern rebels.

sentences.zh: 崇遣其將陸顗渡江，夜，襲六兒，破其兩營，收其器械軍資而去，眾益盛，至十萬。

translations.literal: Chong sent his general Lu Yan to cross the Jiang; by night assaulted Liu'er; broke two camps; gathered their weapons and military stores and departed; the host grew ever stronger—to a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Chong sent his commander Lu Yan across the river. In a night attack he smashed two of Liu'er's camps and carried off weapons and supplies. His force swelled to a hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，司農卿雲陽趙元淑坐楊玄感黨伏誅。

translations.literal: On xinyou, Minister of Revenue Yun Yang Zhao Yuanshu, implicated as Yang Xuangan's partisan, was executed.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou day, Zhao Yuanshu of Yunyang, minister of revenue, was executed as an associate of Yang Xuangan.

sentences.zh: 帝使大理卿鄭善果、御史大夫裴蘊、刑部侍郎骨儀、與留守樊子蓋推玄感黨與。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review Zheng Shanguo, Censor-in-Chief Pei Yun, Vice Minister of Justice Gu Yi, together with garrison commander Fan Zigai to investigate Xuangan's associates.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Chief Judge Zheng Shanguo, Censor Pei Yun, Vice Minister Gu Yi, and Fan Zigai, who held the Eastern Capital, to investigate Xuangan's accomplices.

sentences.zh: 儀，本天竺胡人也。

translations.literal: Yi was originally a man of Tianzhu (India) Hu descent.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Yi was originally of Indian descent.

sentences.zh: 帝謂蘊曰：「玄感一呼而從者十萬，益知天下人不欲多，多即相聚為盜耳。

translations.literal: The emperor said to Yun: "Xuangan one cry and those who followed were a hundred thousand—ever more one knows men under Heaven do not wish to be many; when many, they gather and become bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Pei Yun: "At Xuangan's single call, a hundred thousand followed. It proves my point—the people cannot tolerate overcrowding. Gather too many together and they turn to banditry.

sentences.zh: 不盡加誅，無以懲後。」

translations.literal: If not all are added execution, there is no means to warn those after."
translations.idiomatic: Unless we kill them all, there will be no deterring the next rebellion."

sentences.zh: 子蓋性既殘酷，蘊復受此旨，由是峻法治之，所殺三萬餘人，皆籍沒其家，枉死者太半，流徙者六千餘人。

translations.literal: Zigai's nature was already cruel; Yun again received this charge; thereby harsh law governed them; those killed were thirty thousand-plus; all estates confiscated; more than half wrongfully dead; those banished six thousand-plus.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zigai was brutal by nature, and Pei Yun now had the emperor's mandate. The purge was merciless: more than thirty thousand were killed, their property seized; well over half were innocent, and six thousand more were exiled.

sentences.zh: 玄感之圍東都也，開倉賑給百姓。

translations.literal: When Xuangan besieged the Eastern Capital, he opened granaries to relieve and supply the common people.
translations.idiomatic: During the siege of the Eastern Capital, Xuangan had opened the granaries to feed the people.

sentences.zh: 凡受米者，皆坑之於都城之南。

translations.literal: All who received rice were buried alive south of the capital city.
translations.idiomatic: Every person who had taken grain was buried alive south of the capital.

sentences.zh: 玄感所善文士會稽虞綽、琅邪王冑俱坐徙邊，綽、冑亡命，捕得，誅之。

translations.literal: Literary gentlemen Xuangan favored—Kuaiji's Yu Chuo and Langye's Wang Zhou—both were implicated and banished to the frontier; Chuo and Zhou fled as outlaws; captured; executed.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chuo of Kuaiji and Wang Zhou of Langye, literati whom Xuangan had favored, were sentenced to frontier exile. They fled, were captured, and were put to death.

sentences.zh: 帝善屬文，不欲人出其右。

translations.literal: The emperor was skilled at literary composition; did not wish men to surpass him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was a gifted writer and could not abide rivals.

sentences.zh: 薛道衡死，帝曰：「更能作『空梁落燕泥』否！」

translations.literal: When Xue Daohang died, the emperor said: "Can you still compose 'Empty beams, falling swallow mud'!"
translations.idiomatic: When Xue Daohang was dead, the emperor mocked: "Can he still write 'empty rafters, swallows' mud' now?"

sentences.zh: 王冑死，帝誦其佳句曰：「『庭草無人隨意綠，』復能作此語邪！」

translations.literal: When Wang Zhou died, the emperor recited his fine line: "'Courtyard grass unmanned, at will green'—can he still compose such language!"
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Zhou died, the emperor quoted his best line—"'Unseen, the courtyard grass grows green as it will'"—and sneered: "Can he still write like that?"

sentences.zh: 帝自負才學，每驕天下之士，嘗謂侍臣曰：「天下皆謂朕承藉緒餘而有四海，設令朕與士大夫高選，亦當為天子矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor prided himself on talent and learning; always looked down on the realm's scholars; once said to attending ministers: "All under Heaven say I inherited surplus threads and obtained the Four Seas—suppose I competed in high selection with scholar-officials—I too would have been Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Vain about his own brilliance, the emperor despised the scholars of the realm. He once told his courtiers: "The world thinks I inherited the throne. Had I competed with the finest minds of the land, I would still have become emperor."

sentences.zh: 帝從容謂秘書郎虞世南曰：「我性不喜人諫，若位望通顯而諫以求名者，彌所不耐。

translations.literal: The emperor at ease said to Secretariat Gentleman Yu Shinan: "By nature I do not like men to remonstrate; if one of rank and eminence remonstrates seeking fame—I am all the less able to bear it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said casually to Secretariat Gentleman Yu Shinan: "I do not take well to advice. Officials of rank who counsel me only to burnish their reputations—I find especially unbearable.

sentences.zh: 至於卑賤之士，雖少寬假，然卒不置之地上。

translations.literal: As for lowly scholars—though somewhat more indulgent—in the end I do not place them on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Humble men may receive somewhat more leniency, but in the end I never let them off entirely.

sentences.zh: 汝其知之！」

translations.literal: You ought to know this!"
translations.idiomatic: You would do well to remember that!"

sentences.zh: 世南，世基之弟也。

translations.literal: Shinan was Shiji's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shinan was the younger brother of Yu Shiji.

sentences.zh: 帝使裴矩安集隴右，因之會寧，存問曷薩那可汗部落，遣闕達度設寇掠吐谷渾以自富，還而奏狀，帝大賞之。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Pei Ju to pacify and settle Longyou; on the way at Huining, inquired after the tribes of Khan Hasa Ke; sent Que Dachu She to raid and plunder Tuyuhun to enrich himself; returned and memorialized; the emperor greatly rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Pei Ju to stabilize Longyou. At Huining he paid respects to the tribes of the Qaghan Hasa Ke, then dispatched Que Dachu She to raid Tuyuhun and fill the coffers. When Ju returned with his report, the emperor richly rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 九月，己卯，東海民彭孝才起為盜，有眾數萬。

translations.literal: Ninth month, on jimao, East Sea commoner Peng Xiaocai rose as bandit; had a host of several ten-thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on jimao day, Peng Xiaocai of the East Sea turned bandit with a following of tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 甲午，車駕至上谷，以供費不給，免太守虞荷等官。

translations.literal: On jiawu, the imperial carriage reached Shanggu; because supplies and costs were insufficient, dismissed prefect Yu He and others from office.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu day the imperial procession reached Shanggu. Because local supplies failed to meet demand, Prefect Yu He and others were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 閏月，己巳，幸博陵。

translations.literal: Intercalary month, on jisi, favored visit to Boling.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on jisi day, the emperor visited Boling.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丁丑，賊帥呂明星圍東郡，虎賁郎將費青奴擊破之。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, on dingchou, bandit chief Lu Mingxing besieged Dong commandery; Tiger Fang General Fei Qingnu defeated and broke him.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on dingchou day, the bandit chief Lu Mingxing besieged Dong commandery. General Fei Qingnu of the Tiger Guards routed him.

sentences.zh: 劉元進帥其眾將渡江，會楊玄感敗，朱燮、管崇迎元進，推以為主，據吳郡，稱天子，燮、崇俱為尚書僕射，署置百官，毘陵、東陽、會稽、建安豪傑多執長吏以應之。

translations.literal: Liu Yuanjin led his host about to cross the Jiang; when Xuangan was defeated; Zhu Xie and Guan Chong welcomed Yuanjin; pushed him as master; held Wu commandery; called himself Son of Heaven; Xie and Chong both were Vice Directors of the Masters of Writing; appointed and installed the hundred officials; Piling, Dongyang, Kuaiji, Jian'an worthies many seized chief officials in response.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuanjin was about to cross the Yangtze with his army when Xuangan fell. Zhu Xie and Guan Chong welcomed him, set him up as their leader, seized Wu commandery, and proclaimed him emperor. Xie and Chong became vice premiers; offices were filled across the government. Leading men in Piling, Dongyang, Kuaiji, and Jian'an seized their local officials and joined the cause.

sentences.zh: 帝遣左屯衛大將軍代人吐萬緒、光祿大夫下邽魚俱羅將兵討之。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Left Garrison Guard Grand General Tuyuan Xu of the Dai region, Director of the Palace Officials Yuju Luo of Xia Gui, to lead troops to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched Grand General Tuyuan Xu of the Left Garrison Guard and Palace Official Yuju Luo of Xi Gui to crush the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 十一月，己酉，右候衛將軍馮孝慈討張金稱於清河，孝慈敗死。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, on jiyou, Right Houwei General Feng Xiaoci campaigned against Zhang Jinheng at Qinghe; Xiaoci was defeated and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on jiyou day, General Feng Xiaoci of the Right Houwei Guard attacked Zhang Jinheng in Qinghe—and was defeated and killed.

sentences.zh: 楊玄感之西也，韋福嗣亡詣東都歸首，是時如其比者皆不問。

translations.literal: When Xuangan went west, Wei Fusi fled and went to the Eastern Capital to surrender; at that time such as he were all not prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuangan marched west, Wei Fusi fled to the Eastern Capital and surrendered. Others who did the same were not punished.

sentences.zh: 樊子蓋收玄感文簿，得其書草，封以呈帝；

translations.literal: Fan Zigai collected Xuangan's document registers, obtained his draft writings, sealed them and presented to the emperor;
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zigai seized Xuangan's papers and found among them draft documents, which he sealed and sent to the emperor;

sentences.zh: 帝命執送行在。

translations.literal: the emperor ordered him seized and sent to the traveling encampment.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor ordered Wei Fusi arrested and brought to his camp.

sentences.zh: 李密亡命，為人所獲，亦送東都。

translations.literal: Li Mi was a fugitive; was captured by men; also sent to Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Mi, also a fugitive, was captured and sent to the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 樊子蓋鎖送福嗣、密及楊積善、王仲伯等十餘人詣高陽，密與王仲伯等竊謀亡去，悉使出其所繼金以示使者曰：「吾等死日，此金並留付公，幸用相瘞，其餘即皆報德。」

translations.literal: Fan Zigai under escort sent Fusi, Mi, Yang Jishan, Wang Zhongbo, and a dozen-odd others to Gaoyang; Mi with Wang Zhongbo and others secretly plotted to flee; all produced inherited gold they carried to show the escort: "On the day of our death, this gold all leave to you, sir—pray use it to bury us; the rest is all repaying kindness."
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zigai had Fusi, Mi, Yang Jishan, Wang Zhongbo, and a dozen others chained and sent toward Gaoyang. Mi and Wang Zhongbo plotted escape. They pooled their gold and showed the escorts: "When we die, keep this gold for burying us—and keep the rest as our thanks."

sentences.zh: 使者利其金，許諾，防禁漸弛。

translations.literal: The escorts coveted the gold; promised; guard and confinement gradually slackened.
translations.idiomatic: Greedy for the gold, the escorts agreed, and their watch grew lax.

sentences.zh: 密請通市酒食，每宴飲，喧嘩竟夕，使者不以為意。

translations.literal: Mi requested to buy wine and food in the markets; each feast and drink—noise and clamor until evening; the escorts did not regard it.
translations.idiomatic: Mi began buying wine and food at every stop. Their nightly feasts rang with rowdy laughter until dawn, and the escorts thought nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 行至魏郡石梁驛，飲防守者皆醉，穿牆而逸。

translations.literal: Reaching Wei's commandery Shiliang Post, drinking—the guards all drunk; broke through the wall and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: At Shiliang Post in Wei commandery they got the guards drunk, broke through a wall, and fled.

sentences.zh: 密呼韋福嗣同去，福嗣曰：「我無罪，天子不過一面責我耳。」

translations.literal: Mi called Wei Fusi to go together; Fusi said: "I am without guilt—the Son of Heaven at most will face me and reproach me."
translations.idiomatic: Mi urged Wei Fusi to come along. Fusi refused: "I have done nothing wrong. The worst the emperor will do is scold me to my face."

sentences.zh: 至高陽，帝以書草示福嗣，收付大理。

translations.literal: Reaching Gaoyang, the emperor showed Fusi the draft writings; seized and delivered to the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: At Gaoyang the emperor showed Fusi the incriminating drafts and handed him over to the judiciary.

sentences.zh: 宇文述奏：「凶逆之徒，臣下所當同疾，若不為重法，無以肅將來。」

translations.literal: Yuwen Shu memorialized: "Fierce rebellious fellows—ministers and subordinates should share hatred; if heavy law is not applied, there is no means to awe the future."
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Shu urged: "Traitors such as these are enemies to every loyal subject. Unless we make an example of them, rebellion will never end."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「聽公所為。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I heed what you, sir, do."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Do as you see fit."

sentences.zh: 十二月，甲申，述就野外，縛諸應刑者於格上，以車輪括其頸，使文武九品以上皆持兵斫射，亂髮矢如□胃毛，支體糜碎，猶在車輪中。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, on jiashen, Shu at the open countryside bound all who should suffer punishment on frames; used cart wheels to brace their necks; made civil and military officials of the ninth rank and above all hold weapons to hack and shoot; scattered arrows like hedgehog quills; limbs pulverized—still within the cart wheels.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on jiashen day, Yuwen Shu bound the condemned in the open field, wedging their necks in cart wheels. He ordered every official from the ninth rank upward to hack and shoot at them. Arrows flew thick as hedgehog bristles until their flesh was pulp—yet they still hung in the wheels.

sentences.zh: 積善、福嗣仍加車裂，皆焚而揚之。

translations.literal: Jishan and Fusi additionally had splitting by cart; all were burned and their ashes scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Jishan and Fusi were further torn apart by chariots; all were burned and their ashes cast to the wind.

sentences.zh: 積善自言手殺玄感，冀得免死。

translations.literal: Jishan himself said he had personally killed Xuangan; hoped to obtain exemption from death.
translations.idiomatic: Jishan claimed he had killed Xuangan with his own hand, hoping to escape death.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「然則梟類耳！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Then he is owl-kind only!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Then he is no better than an owl!"

sentences.zh: 因更其姓曰梟氏。

translations.literal: Therefore changed his surname to Owl Clan.
translations.idiomatic: And had his surname changed to Owl.

sentences.zh: 唐縣人宋子賢，善幻術，能變佛形，自稱彌勒出世，遠近信惑，遂謀因無遮大會舉兵襲乘輿；

translations.literal: Tang county man Song Zixian was skilled at illusion arts; could transform into Buddha form; himself called Maitreya descended to the world; near and far believed and were deluded; then plotted by the Unhindered Great Assembly to raise troops and surprise the imperial carriage;
translations.idiomatic: Song Zixian of Tang county was a master of illusion who could appear in the form of the Buddha. Proclaiming himself Maitreya reborn, he won believers far and wide and plotted to attack the emperor during the Unhindered Assembly;

sentences.zh: 事洩，伏誅，並誅黨與千餘家。

translations.literal: The affair leaked; was executed; together executed associates—a thousand-plus households.
translations.idiomatic: The plot was discovered; he was executed, along with more than a thousand families of his followers.

sentences.zh: 扶風桑門向海明亦自稱彌勒出世，人有歸心者，輒獲吉夢，由是三輔人翕然奉之，因舉兵反，眾至數萬。

translations.literal: Fufeng monk Xiang Haiming also called himself Maitreya descended; whoever had a returning heart obtained auspicious dreams; thereby people of the Three Adjuncts uniformly honored him; then raised troops in rebellion; host reached several ten-thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Xiang Haiming of Fufeng also claimed to be Maitreya. Those who joined him dreamed lucky dreams, and the people of the Three Adjuncts rallied to him by the thousands. He rebelled with an army of tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，海明自稱皇帝，改元白烏。

translations.literal: On dinghai, Haiming called himself emperor; changed era to White Crow.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai day he proclaimed himself emperor under the era name White Crow.

sentences.zh: 詔太僕卿楊義臣擊破之。

translations.literal: An edict: Grand Master of the Imperial Stud Yang Yichen defeated and broke him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Grand Master Yang Yichen to defeat him—and Yichen did.

sentences.zh: 帝召衛文升、樊子蓋詣行在；

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Wei Wensheng and Fan Zigai to the traveling encampment;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Wei Wensheng and Fan Zigai to his camp;

sentences.zh: 慰勞之，賞賜極厚，遣還所任。

translations.literal: consoled and labored them; rewards extremely generous; sent back to their posts.
translations.idiomatic: praised them lavishly, rewarded them richly, and sent them back to their posts.

sentences.zh: 劉元進攻丹楊，吐萬緒濟江擊破之，元進解圍去，緒進屯曲阿。

translations.literal: Liu Yuanjin attacked Danyang; Tuyuan Xu crossed the Jiang, defeated and broke him; Yuanjin lifted siege and departed; Xu advanced and encamped at Qu'e.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuanjin attacked Danyang. Tuyuan Xu crossed the Yangtze and routed him. Yuanjin broke off the siege and fled; Xu advanced and encamped at Qu'e.

sentences.zh: 元進結柵拒緒，相持百餘日；

translations.literal: Yuanjin built palisades to resist Xu; stalemate of a hundred-plus days;
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjin fortified his lines against Xu, and the two armies faced each other for more than a hundred days;

sentences.zh: 緒擊之，賊眾大潰，死者以萬數。

translations.literal: Xu struck them; the bandit host greatly routed; the dead numbered by ten-thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Xu attacked and the rebel army collapsed; the dead were counted in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 元進挺身夜遁，保其壘。

translations.literal: Yuanjin straightened his body and fled by night, holding his fort.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjin slipped away under cover of night and held his fortified camp.

sentences.zh: 朱燮、管崇等屯毘陵，連營百餘里，緒乘勝進擊，復破之。

translations.literal: Zhu Xie, Guan Chong, and others encamped at Piling, linked camps for a hundred-plus li; Xu pressed the victory and advanced to strike, again breaking them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xie and Guan Chong had encamped at Piling in a chain of fortifications stretching more than a hundred li. Xu pressed his advantage, attacked again, and routed them once more.

sentences.zh: 賊退保黃山，緒圍之，元進、燮僅以身免，於陳斬崇及其將卒五個餘人，收其子女三萬餘口，進解會稽圍。

translations.literal: The bandits retreated to hold Huang Mountain; Xu besieged them; Yuanjin and Xie barely escaped with their persons; on the battlefield beheaded Chong and his generals and soldiers five-plus ten-thousands; collected their women and children thirty thousand-plus mouths; advanced and lifted the siege of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fell back to Huang Mountain, where Xu besieged them. Yuanjin and Xie escaped with their lives alone. On the field Xu beheaded Chong and more than fifty thousand of his officers and men, took more than thirty thousand women and children captive, and marched on to raise the siege of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 魚俱羅與緒偕行，戰無不捷，然百姓從亂者如歸市，賊敗而復聚，其勢益盛。

translations.literal: Yu Juluo marched together with Xu; in battle none were not victorious—yet commoners joining rebellion were like returning to market; bandits defeated yet again gathered; their momentum grew ever stronger.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Juluo campaigned alongside Xu, and every battle went their way. Yet the people flocking to rebellion came as thick as shoppers at a market—defeated bands regrouped, and the movement only grew stronger.

sentences.zh: 元進退據建安，帝令緒進討，緒以士卒疲弊，請息甲待來春，帝不悅。

translations.literal: Yuanjin retreated to hold Jian'an; the emperor ordered Xu to advance and suppress; Xu, because troops and horses were worn and exhausted, requested to rest armor and wait until next spring; the emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjin withdrew to Jian'an. The emperor ordered Xu to press the attack, but Xu, finding his men exhausted, asked to stand down until spring. The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 俱羅亦以賊非歲月可平，諸子在洛京，潛遣家僕迎之；

translations.literal: Juluo also thought the bandits could not be pacified within months; his sons were in Luoyang; secretly sent household servants to welcome them;
translations.idiomatic: Juluo too believed the rebels could not be crushed in a matter of months. His sons were in Luoyang, and he secretly sent household servants to fetch them;

sentences.zh: 帝怒。

translations.literal: The emperor grew angry.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 有司希旨，奏緒怯懦，俱羅敗衄，俱羅坐斬，徵緒詣行在，緒憂憤，道卒。

translations.literal: Officials seeking to please the imperial intent memorialized that Xu was cowardly; Juluo had suffered defeat; Juluo was sentenced to decapitation; Xu was summoned to the traveling encampment; Xu, grieved and indignant, died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Officials eager to please the throne reported that Xu was timid and Juluo had been routed. Juluo was executed, and Xu was recalled to the emperor's camp. Overcome with grief and anger, Xu died on the journey.

sentences.zh: 帝更遣江都丞王世充發淮南兵數萬人討元進。

translations.literal: The emperor again dispatched Jiangdu assistant prefect Wang Shichong to raise several ten-thousands of Huainan troops to suppress Yuanjin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Jiangdu's assistant prefect Wang Shichong with tens of thousands of Huainan troops against Yuanjin.

sentences.zh: 世充渡江，頻戰皆捷，元進、燮敗死於吳，其餘眾或降或散。

translations.literal: Shichong crossed the Jiang; frequent battles all victorious; Yuanjin and Xie were defeated and died in Wu; the remaining host either surrendered or scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong crossed the Yangtze and won battle after battle. Yuanjin and Xie were defeated and killed in Wu, and the rest of their followers either surrendered or melted away.

sentences.zh: 世充召先降者於通玄寺瑞像前焚香為誓，約降者不殺。

translations.literal: Shichong summoned those who had surrendered earlier before the auspicious image at Tongxuan Temple, burned incense to make oath, covenanting that those who surrendered would not be killed.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong gathered earlier defectors before the sacred image at Tongxuan Temple, burned incense, and swore that those who surrendered would not be harmed.

sentences.zh: 散者始欲入海為盜，聞之，旬月之間，歸首略盡，世充悉坑之於黃亭澗，死者三萬餘人。

translations.literal: Those scattered at first wished to go to sea and become bandits; hearing this, within ten days and a month returning heads were nearly exhausted; Shichong all buried alive them at Huangting Stream; the dead were thirty thousand-plus men.
translations.idiomatic: Dispersed rebels who had planned to take to the sea heard the promise, and within a month nearly all came in to surrender. Shichong had every one of them buried alive at Huangting Stream—more than thirty thousand dead.

sentences.zh: 由是餘黨復相聚為盜，官軍不能討，以至隋亡。

translations.literal: From this the remaining partisans again gathered to become bandits; government troops could not suppress them—until Sui perished.
translations.idiomatic: After that, surviving rebels banded together again, and the imperial armies could not root them out—a disorder that endured until the fall of Sui.

sentences.zh: 帝以世充有將帥才，益加寵任。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Shichong had general-and-marshal talent, further increased favor and trust.
translations.idiomatic: Impressed by Shichong's talent as a commander, the emperor lavished still greater favor upon him.

sentences.zh: 是歲，詔為盜者籍沒其家。

translations.literal: This year, an edict: for those who became bandits, register and confiscate their households.
translations.idiomatic: That year an edict ordered the property of anyone who turned bandit to be confiscated and his household registered for punishment.

sentences.zh: 時群盜所在皆滿，群縣官因之各專威福，生殺任情矣。

translations.literal: At the time bandits everywhere were full; county and district officials by this each monopolized authority and blessing; life and death followed their whim.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits swarmed in every quarter, and local officials seized the chance to wield unchecked power, killing or sparing as they pleased.

sentences.zh: 章丘杜伏威與臨濟輔公祏為刎頸交，俱亡命為群盜。

translations.literal: Zhangqiu Du Fuwei and Linji Fu Gongshi were sworn friends unto death; both fled as outlaws and became bandit chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Du Fuwei of Zhangqiu and Fu Gongshi of Linji were sworn brothers in exile, both having taken to the hills as outlaws.

sentences.zh: 伏威年十六，每出則居前，入則殿後，由是其徒推以為帥。

translations.literal: Fuwei was sixteen years old; whenever going out he went in front, entering he guarded the rear; by this his followers pushed him to be commander.
translations.idiomatic: Fuwei was only sixteen, yet on every raid he marched at the head and covered the rear on withdrawal. His band made him their leader.

sentences.zh: 下邳苗海潮亦聚眾為盜，伏威使公祏謂之曰：「今我與君同苦隋政，各舉大義，力分勢弱，常恐被擒。

translations.literal: Xiapi Miao Haichao also gathered a host as bandits; Fuwei sent Gongshi to tell him: "Now you and I alike suffer Sui government; each raises great righteousness; strength divided, momentum weak—we constantly fear capture.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Haichao of Xiapi had also raised a band of rebels. Fuwei sent Gongshi to tell him: "We both suffer under Sui rule and have each taken up arms, but divided we are weak and easily captured.

sentences.zh: 若合為一，則足以敵隋矣。

translations.literal: If we unite as one, then it suffices to oppose Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Unite with us, and together we can stand against Sui.

sentences.zh: 君能為主，吾當敬從，自揆不堪，宜來聽命；

translations.literal: If you, sir, can be leader, I shall respectfully follow; judging myself unfit, you ought to come and heed commands;
translations.idiomatic: If you can lead, I will follow gladly. If you find me the better choice, come and take orders under me;

sentences.zh: 不則一戰以決雌雄。」

translations.literal: otherwise one battle to decide victor and defeated."
translations.idiomatic: otherwise let one battle decide who commands."

sentences.zh: 海潮懼，即帥其眾降之。

translations.literal: Haichao feared; immediately led his host to surrender to him.
translations.idiomatic: Haichao was terrified and brought his followers over at once.

sentences.zh: 伏威轉掠淮南，自稱將軍，江都留守遣校尉宋顥討之，伏威與戰，陽為不勝，引顥眾入葭葦中，因從上風縱火，顥眾皆燒死。

translations.literal: Fuwei turned to plunder Huainan, called himself general; Jiangdu garrison commander sent Commandant Song Hao to suppress him; Fuwei fought, feigning defeat, drew Hao's host into reeds and rushes, then from upwind set fire; Hao's host all burned to death.
translations.idiomatic: Fuwei swept through Huainan proclaiming himself a general. The Jiangdu garrison sent Commandant Song Hao against him. Fuwei feigned defeat, lured Hao's men into the reeds, and set the marsh ablaze from upwind. Hao's entire force burned alive.

sentences.zh: 海陵賊帥趙破陳以伏威兵少，輕之，召與並力；

translations.literal: Hailing bandit chief Zhao Pochen, because Fuwei's troops were few, treated him lightly, summoned him to combine strength;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Pochen, a rebel leader at Hailing, despised Fuwei for his small numbers and invited him to join forces;

sentences.zh: 伏威使公祏嚴兵居外，自與左右十人繼牛酒入謁，於座殺破陳，並其眾。

translations.literal: Fuwei sent Gongshi to array troops sternly outside; himself with a dozen attendants followed with oxen and wine to pay visit; at the seat killed Pochen and absorbed his host.
translations.idiomatic: Fuwei posted Gongshi with armed men outside, then entered with ten companions bearing oxen and wine as gifts—and killed Pochen at the banquet table, absorbing his band.

sentences.zh: 春，二月，辛未，詔百僚議伐高麗，數日，無敢言者。

translations.literal: Spring, second month, day xinwei: edict for hundred officials to discuss attacking Goguryeo; several days—none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the xinwei day of the second month, the emperor ordered the court to debate another campaign against Goguryeo. For days not a soul spoke up.

sentences.zh: 戊子，詔復徵天下兵，百道俱進。

translations.literal: On wuzi, edict again to levy troops from all under Heaven; a hundred routes all advancing together.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi day an edict went out to levy troops across the empire once more, advancing on a hundred fronts.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，扶風賊帥唐弼立李弘芝為天子，有眾十萬，自稱唐王。

translations.literal: On dingyou, Fufeng bandit chief Tang Bi set up Li Hongzhi as Son of Heaven; had a host of a hundred thousand; called himself King of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou day Tang Bi of Fufeng proclaimed Li Hongzhi emperor before a host of a hundred thousand and styled himself King of Tang.

sentences.zh: 三月，壬子，帝行幸涿郡，士卒在道，亡者相繼。

translations.literal: Third month, day renzi: the emperor traveled in progress to Zhuo commandery; soldiers on the road, deserters followed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on renzi day, the emperor set out for Zhuo commandery. Soldiers deserted along the march in an unbroken stream.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，至臨渝宮，榪祭黃帝，斬叛軍者以釁鼓，亡者亦不止。

translations.literal: On guihai, reached Linyu Palace; performed ma sacrifice to Yellow Emperor; beheaded deserters to smear the drums; deserters still did not stop.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai day he reached Linyu Palace, offered the ma sacrifice to the Yellow Emperor, and beheaded deserters to consecrate the war drums—but the flight of troops did not cease.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，榆林太守成紀董純與彭城賊帥張大虎戰於昌慮，大破之，斬首萬餘級。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month: Yulin prefect Chengji Dong Chun fought Pengcheng bandit chief Zhang Dahu at Changlu, greatly broke him, beheaded ten thousand-plus heads.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Yulin's prefect Dong Chun of Chengji fought Zhang Dahu of Pengcheng at Changlu, routed him, and took more than ten thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 甲午，車駕至北平。

translations.literal: On jiawu, the imperial carriage reached Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu day the imperial procession arrived at Beiping.

sentences.zh: 五月，庚申，延安賊帥劉迦論自稱皇王，建元大世，有眾十萬，與稽胡相表裡為寇。

translations.literal: Fifth month, day gengshen: Yan'an bandit chief Liu Jialun called himself August King, established era Great Age, had a host of a hundred thousand; with Ji Hu acted inside and outside as raiders.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on gengshen day, Liu Jialun of Yan'an proclaimed himself emperor under the era name Great Age, mustered a hundred thousand men, and coordinated raids with the Ji Hu tribes.

sentences.zh: 詔以左驍衛大將軍屈突通為關內討捕大使，發兵擊之，戰於上郡，斬迦論並將卒萬餘級，虜男女數萬口而還。

translations.literal: Edict appointing Left Xiaowei Grand General Qu Tutong as Guannei suppression-and-capture commissioner; raised troops to strike; fought at Shang commandery; beheaded Jialun together with generals and soldiers ten thousand-plus heads; captured men and women several ten-thousands of mouths and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Qu Tutong, Grand General of the Left Xiaowei Guard, commissioner to suppress bandits in Guannei. Tutong gave battle in Shang commandery, killed Jialun along with more than ten thousand of his officers and men, and returned with tens of thousands of captives.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，癸丑，車駕次懷遠鎮。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, day guichou: the imperial carriage halted at Huaiyuan garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, on the guichou day of the seventh month, the imperial procession halted at Huaiyuan garrison.

sentences.zh: 時天下已亂，所徵兵多失期不至，高麗亦困弊。

translations.literal: At the time all under Heaven was already in disorder; levied troops mostly missed deadlines and did not arrive; Goguryeo too was exhausted and depleted.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was already in turmoil. Levied troops failed to arrive on time in great numbers, and Goguryeo too was worn to the bone.

sentences.zh: 來護兒至畢奢城，高麗舉兵逆戰，護兒擊破之，將趣平壤，高麗王元懼，甲子，遣使乞降，囚送斛斯政。

translations.literal: Lai Huer reached Bishe city; Goguryeo raised troops to oppose battle; Huer struck and broke them, was about to press toward Pyongyang; Goguryeo King Yuan feared; on jiazi sent envoys begging surrender, imprisoned and sent Husi Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Huer reached Bishe city, where Goguryeo met him in battle. Huer routed the enemy and was advancing on Pyongyang when King Yuan of Goguryeo, terrified, sent envoys on jiazi day to sue for peace and delivered Husi Zheng in chains.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，遣使持節召護兒還。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly rejoiced; dispatched envoys bearing staff of authority to summon Huer back.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and sent envoys with imperial credentials ordering Huer to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 護兒集眾曰：「大軍三出，未能平賊，此還不可復來。

translations.literal: Huer assembled the host and said: "The great army has thrice gone forth and could not pacify the enemy; if we return now we cannot come again.
translations.idiomatic: Huer assembled his troops and said: "The empire has sent three great armies and still failed to crush them. If we turn back now, we may never get another chance.

sentences.zh: 勞而無功，吾竊恥之。

translations.literal: To labor yet gain no merit—I privately am shamed by this.
translations.idiomatic: To toil without victory is a shame I cannot bear.

sentences.zh: 今高麗實困，以此眾擊之，不日可克。

translations.literal: Now Goguryeo is truly exhausted; with this host to strike them, within days it can be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo is truly at the end of its strength. With this army we can finish them in days.

sentences.zh: 吾欲進兵徑圍平壤，聚高元，獻捷而歸，不亦善乎！」

translations.literal: I wish to advance troops directly to besiege Pyongyang, gather Gao Yuan, present victory and return—is this not good!"
translations.idiomatic: I mean to march straight on Pyongyang, seize Gao Yuan, and return in triumph—would that not be better!"

sentences.zh: 答表請行，不肯奉詔。

translations.literal: He replied in memorial requesting to proceed, refused to obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized asking leave to advance and refused to obey the recall.

sentences.zh: 長吏崔君肅固爭，護兒不可，曰：「賊勢破矣，獨以相任，自足辦之。

translations.literal: Chief clerk Cui Junsu firmly remonstrated; Huer would not agree, saying: "The enemy's momentum is broken; entrusted alone to me, it suffices to handle.
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerk Cui Junsu argued fiercely against him, but Huer would not listen. "The enemy is broken," he said. "The emperor has entrusted this to me alone, and I am equal to it.

sentences.zh: 吾在閫外，事當專決，寧得高元還而獲譴，捨此成功，所不能矣！」

translations.literal: I am outside the barbican gate; affairs ought to be decided exclusively—better to bring Gao Yuan back and receive censure than abandon this success; that I cannot do!"
translations.idiomatic: A general in the field decides for himself. I would rather bring Gao Yuan back in chains and face punishment than throw away certain victory—that I cannot do!"

sentences.zh: 君肅告眾曰：「若從元帥違拒詔書，必當聞奏，皆應獲罪。」

translations.literal: Junsu told the host: "If you follow the commander in defying and refusing the edict, it will surely be reported to the throne—all should receive guilt."
translations.idiomatic: Junsu warned the army: "If you follow the commander in defying the imperial edict, I will report this to the throne, and every one of you will be punished."

sentences.zh: 諸將懼，俱請還，乃始奉詔。

translations.literal: The generals feared; all requested return; only then did he begin to obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: The officers were terrified, all pleaded to withdraw, and only then did Huer obey the recall.

sentences.zh: 八月，己巳，帝自懷遠鎮班師。

translations.literal: Eighth month, day jisi: the emperor withdrew the army from Huaiyuan garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on jisi day, the emperor withdrew his army from Huaiyuan garrison.

sentences.zh: 邯鄲賊帥楊公卿帥其黨八千人抄駕後第八隊，得飛黃上廄馬四十二匹而去。

translations.literal: Handan bandit chief Yang Gongqing led his partisans eight thousand men to raid the eighth company behind the imperial progress; obtained forty-two Feihuang upper-stable horses and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gongqing of Handan led eight thousand followers in a raid on the eighth company trailing the imperial procession, seized forty-two of the palace's finest steeds, and escaped.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丁卯，上至東都；

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day dingmao: the emperor reached the Eastern Capital;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, on the dingmao day of the tenth month, the emperor reached the Eastern Capital;

sentences.zh: 己丑，還西京。

translations.literal: On jichou, returned to the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: on jichou day he returned to the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 以高麗使者及斛斯政告太廟；

translations.literal: Presented Goguryeo envoys and Husi Zheng to the Imperial Ancestral Temple;
translations.idiomatic: He presented the Goguryeo envoys and Husi Zheng before the Imperial Ancestral Temple;

sentences.zh: 仍徵高麗王元入朝，元竟不至。

translations.literal: still summoned Goguryeo King Yuan to court; Yuan in the end did not come.
translations.idiomatic: and summoned King Yuan of Goguryeo to court—but Yuan never came.

sentences.zh: 敕將帥嚴裝，更圖後舉，竟不果行。

translations.literal: Ordered generals and marshals to prepare arms strictly, again to plan a later campaign—ultimately it did not come to pass.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his commanders to stand ready for another campaign, but in the end nothing came of it.

sentences.zh: 初，開皇之末，國家殷盛，朝野皆以高麗為意，劉炫獨以為不可，作《撫夷論》以刺之，至是，其言始驗。

translations.literal: Initially, at the end of Kaihuang, the state was abundant and flourishing; court and countryside all set mind on Goguryeo; Liu Xuan alone thought it impossible; composed "Treatise on Pacifying the Barbarians" to satirize this—by now his words first were verified.
translations.idiomatic: In the prosperous closing years of Emperor Wen's Kaihuang era, court and country alike had Goguryeo on the mind. Only Liu Xuan dissented, writing his Treatise on Pacifying the Barbarians in protest. Now at last his warning had come true.

sentences.zh: 十一月，丙申，殺斛斯政於金光門外，如楊積善之法，仍烹其肉，使百官啖之，佞者或啖之至飽，收其餘骨，焚而揚之。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, day bingshen: killed Husi Zheng outside Jinguang Gate, by the method used on Yang Jishan; still boiled his flesh, made hundred officials eat it; flatterers some ate until full; collected the remaining bones, burned and scattered them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on bingshen day, Husi Zheng was executed outside Jinguang Gate in the same manner as Yang Jishan. His flesh was boiled and the officials forced to eat it—sycophants gorged themselves. The bones that remained were gathered, burned, and cast to the wind.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，有事於南郊，上不齋於次。

translations.literal: On yisi, performed rites at the Southern Suburb; the emperor did not fast at the lodge.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi day rites were performed at the Southern Suburb, but the emperor did not observe the fasting retreat beforehand.

sentences.zh: 詰朝，備法駕，至即行禮。

translations.literal: At dawn, prepared the imperial carriage and escort; upon arrival immediately performed the rites.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he assembled the full imperial procession, arrived, and performed the ceremony at once.

sentences.zh: 是日，大風。

translations.literal: That day, great wind.
translations.idiomatic: That day a fierce wind blew.

sentences.zh: 上獨獻上帝，三公分獻五帝。

translations.literal: The emperor alone offered to Supreme God; the Three Dukes separately offered to the Five Emperors.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor alone made offering to Supreme Heaven; the Three Dukes each offered to one of the Five Emperors.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，御馬疾驅而歸。

translations.literal: When rites were complete, mounted horse and galloped swiftly back.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were finished, he galloped back on horseback without delay.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，離石胡劉苗王反，自稱天子，眾至數萬；

translations.literal: On yimao, Lishi Hu Liu Miaowang rebelled, called himself Son of Heaven; host reached several ten-thousands;
translations.idiomatic: On yimao day Liu Miaowang of the Lishi Hu rebelled, proclaimed himself emperor, and gathered tens of thousands;

sentences.zh: 將軍潘長文討之，不克。

translations.literal: General Pan Changwen suppressed him, could not overcome.
translations.idiomatic: General Pan Changwen was sent against him but could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 汲郡賊帥王德仁擁眾數萬，保林慮山為盜。

translations.literal: Jijun bandit chief Wang Deren held a host of several ten-thousands, defended Mount Linlu as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Deren of Jijun mustered tens of thousands and held Mount Linlu as an outlaw stronghold.

sentences.zh: 帝將如東都，太史令庚質諫曰：「比歲伐遼，民實勞弊，陛下宜鎮撫關內，使百姓盡力農桑，三五年間，四海稍豐實，然後巡省，於事為宜。」

translations.literal: The emperor was about to go to the Eastern Capital; Grand Astrologer Geng Zhi remonstrated: "In recent years attacking Liaodong, the people are truly worn and exhausted; Your Majesty ought to pacify and soothe Guanzhong, make commoners exert themselves fully in farming and sericulture; within three to five years, the four seas will gradually be abundant and solid—then make inspection tours; for affairs this is fitting."
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor prepared to travel to the Eastern Capital, Grand Astrologer Geng Zhi remonstrated: "These repeated campaigns against Liaodong have exhausted the people. Your Majesty should settle Guanzhong and let the farmers return to their fields. In three or five years the realm may grow prosperous again—then a tour would be fitting."

sentences.zh: 帝不悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 質辭疾不從，帝怒，下質獄，竟死獄中。

translations.literal: Zhi pleaded illness and would not follow; the emperor grew angry, cast Zhi into prison; in the end died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Geng pleaded illness and refused to accompany him. The emperor in fury had him imprisoned, and there Geng died.

sentences.zh: 十二月，壬申，帝如東都，赦天下；

translations.literal: Twelfth month, day renshen: the emperor went to the Eastern Capital; amnestied all under Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on renshen day, the emperor traveled to the Eastern Capital and proclaimed a general amnesty;

sentences.zh: 戊子，入東都。

translations.literal: On wuzi, entered the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: on wuzi day he entered the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 東海賊帥彭孝才轉掠沂水，彭城留守董純討擒之。

translations.literal: Donghai bandit chief Peng Xiaocai turned to plunder Yishui; Pengcheng garrison commander Dong Chun suppressed and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Xiaocai of Donghai raided along the Yishui River until Dong Chun, garrison commander of Pengcheng, hunted him down and captured him.

sentences.zh: 純戰雖屢捷，而盜賊日滋，或譖純怯懦；

translations.literal: Chun in battle though repeatedly victorious, yet bandits and robbers daily increased; some slandered Chun as cowardly;
translations.idiomatic: Though Chun won battle after battle, banditry only spread, and some at court slandered him as timid;

sentences.zh: 帝怒，鎖純詣東都，誅之。

translations.literal: The emperor grew angry, chained Chun and sent to the Eastern Capital, executed him.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor in anger had Chun shackled, brought to the Eastern Capital, and executed.

sentences.zh: 孟讓自長白山寇掠諸郡，至盱眙，眾十餘萬，據都梁宮，阻淮為固。

translations.literal: Meng Rang from Changbai Mountain raided and plundered various commanderies; reached Xuyi; host a hundred thousand-plus; held Dulang Palace; blocked the Huai as defense.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Rang, operating from Changbai Mountain, raided commanderies across the region until he reached Xuyi with more than a hundred thousand men, seized Dulang Palace, and fortified his position along the Huai.

sentences.zh: 江都丞王世充將兵拒之，為五柵以塞險要，羸形示弱。

translations.literal: Jiangdu assistant prefect Wang Shichong led troops to resist; made five palisades to block strategic points; showed weak form to display weakness.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong of Jiangdu marched against him, built five palisades to hold the passes, and deliberately appeared weak.

sentences.zh: 讓笑曰：「世充文法小吏，安能將兵！

translations.literal: Rang laughed and said: "Shichong is a petty clerk versed in documents—how can he command troops!
translations.idiomatic: Rang laughed and said: "Shichong is a clerk who knows only paperwork—what does he know of war!

sentences.zh: 吾今生縛取，鼓行入江都耳！」

translations.literal: I today will bind and take him alive, drum-march into Jiangdu—that is all!"
translations.idiomatic: I'll bind him alive today and march straight into Jiangdu!"

sentences.zh: 時民皆結堡自固，野無所掠，賊眾漸餒，乃少留兵，圍五柵，分人於南方抄掠；

translations.literal: At the time commoners all fortified stockades to hold themselves secure; in the wilds nothing to plunder; the bandit host gradually hungered; then left few troops, besieged the five palisades, divided men to the south to raid and plunder;
translations.idiomatic: The people had all fortified their villages, leaving nothing to loot in the countryside. Meng Rang's army grew hungry. He left a small force to besiege the five palisades and sent parties south to forage;

sentences.zh: 世充伺其懈，縱兵出擊，大破之，讓以數十騎遁去，斬首萬餘級。

translations.literal: Shichong watched for their slackness, released troops to strike out, greatly broke them; Rang with several tens of riders fled away; beheaded ten thousand-plus heads.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong waited until they slackened, then sallied forth and routed them. Rang escaped with a few dozen horsemen; more than ten thousand heads were taken.

sentences.zh: 齊郡賊帥左孝友眾十萬屯蹲狗山，郡丞張須陀列營逼之，孝友窘迫出降。

translations.literal: Qi commandery bandit chief Zuo Xiaoyou, host a hundred thousand, encamped at Squatting Dog Mountain; assistant prefect Zhang Xutuo arrayed camps to press him; Xiaoyou, cornered, came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Xiaoyou of Qi commandery held Squatting Dog Mountain with a hundred thousand men. Assistant prefect Zhang Xutuo pressed him with encircling camps until Xiaoyou, trapped, surrendered.

sentences.zh: 須陀威振東夏，以功遷齊郡通守，領河南道十二郡黜陟討捕大使。

translations.literal: Xutuo's authority shook Eastern Xia; by merit was transferred to Qi commandery communications-guardian; led Henan Circuit twelve commanderies promotion-and-dismissal suppression commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Xutuo's fame shook the eastern provinces. For his victories he was made communications-guardian of Qi commandery and commissioner over twelve Henan commanderies with authority to appoint, dismiss, and suppress bandits.

sentences.zh: 涿郡賊帥盧明月眾十餘萬軍祝阿，須陀將萬人邀之。

translations.literal: Zhuo commandery bandit chief Lu Mingyue, host a hundred thousand-plus, encamped at Zhua; Xutuo led ten thousand men to intercept.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Mingyue of Zhuo commandery camped at Zhua with more than a hundred thousand followers. Xutuo met him with ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 相持十餘日，糧盡，將退，謂將士曰：「賊見吾退，必悉眾來追，若以千人襲據其營，可有大利。

translations.literal: Stalemate of ten-plus days; grain exhausted; about to withdraw; told officers and soldiers: "When bandits see us retreat, they will surely bring all their host to pursue; if a thousand men strike and seize their camp, there can be great profit.
translations.idiomatic: After more than ten days their provisions ran out and Xutuo prepared to withdraw. He told his men: "When the enemy sees us retreat, they will pursue in full force. Send a thousand men to seize their camp and the gain will be great.

sentences.zh: 此誠危事，誰能往者？」

translations.literal: This is truly a perilous affair—who can go?"
translations.idiomatic: It is a dangerous mission—who will go?"

sentences.zh: 眾莫對，唯羅士信及歷城秦叔寶請行。

translations.literal: None answered; only Luo Shixin and Licheng Qin Shubao requested to go.
translations.idiomatic: No one spoke until Luo Shixin and Qin Shubao of Licheng volunteered.

sentences.zh: 於是須陀委柵而遁，使二人分將千兵伏葭葦中，明月悉眾追之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xutuo abandoned the palisade and fled; sent the two men each to lead a thousand troops hidden in reeds and rushes; Mingyue with all his host pursued.
translations.idiomatic: Xutuo then abandoned camp and withdrew, while the two men each led a thousand men into ambush among the reeds. Mingyue pursued with his entire force.

sentences.zh: 士信、叔寶馳至其柵，柵門閉，二人超升其樓，各殺數人，營中大亂；

translations.literal: Shixin and Shubao galloped to their palisade; the gate was closed; the two leaped up its tower, each killed several men; the camp fell into great disorder;
translations.idiomatic: Shixin and Shubao raced to the enemy camp. The gate was shut, so the two scaled the tower, each killing several men, and threw the camp into chaos;

sentences.zh: 二人斬關以納外兵，因縱火焚其三十餘柵，煙焰漲天。

translations.literal: The two cut through the gate to admit outside troops; then set fire and burned their thirty-plus palisades; smoke and flames filled the sky.
translations.idiomatic: they cut down the gate to let the main force in and set fire to more than thirty palisades until smoke blotted out the sky.

sentences.zh: 明月奔還，須陀回軍奮擊，大破之，明月以數百騎遁去，所俘斬無算。

translations.literal: Mingyue ran back; Xutuo turned the army and struck fiercely, greatly broke them; Mingyue with several hundred riders fled away; captives and beheadings beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Mingyue raced back, but Xutuo wheeled and struck. The rebel army was shattered; Mingyue fled with a few hundred horsemen. Captives and slain were beyond count.

sentences.zh: 叔寶名瓊，以字行。

translations.literal: Shubao's given name was Qiong; he went by his style name.
translations.idiomatic: Shubao's given name was Qiong, but he was known by his style name.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，增秘書省官百二十員，並以學士補之。

translations.literal: Spring, first month: increased Secretariat officials by a hundred twenty posts; all filled by academicians.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, the Secretariat was expanded by a hundred and twenty posts, all filled from the ranks of imperial academicians.

sentences.zh: 帝好讀書著述，自為揚州總管，置正府學士至百人，常令修撰，以至為帝，前後近二十載，修撰未嘗暫停；

translations.literal: The emperor loved reading books and composing writings; from when he was Yangzhou regional inspector, established chief-office academicians up to a hundred men, constantly ordered compilation; until becoming emperor, nearly twenty years before and after—compilation never paused briefly;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor loved reading and writing. From his days as regional inspector of Yangzhou he had kept as many as a hundred scholars compiling texts for him, and for nearly twenty years as emperor the work never stopped;

sentences.zh: 自經術、文章、兵、農、地理、醫、卜、釋、道乃至蒱博、鷹狗，皆為新書，無不精洽，共成三十一部，萬七千餘卷。

translations.literal: From classics and learning, literature, military affairs, agriculture, geography, medicine, divination, Buddhism, Daoism—even to gambling and hawking—all became new books; none not refined and thorough; together formed thirty-one parts, seventeen thousand-plus scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: covering classics, literature, warfare, agriculture, geography, medicine, divination, Buddhism, Daoism—even gambling and falconry. Nothing was omitted. The result was thirty-one works totaling more than seventeen thousand scrolls.

sentences.zh: 初，西京嘉則殿有書三十七萬卷，帝命秘書監柳顧言等詮次，除其復重猥雜，得正御本三萬七千餘卷，納於東都修文殿。

translations.literal: Initially, the Western Capital's Jiaze Hall had books three hundred seventy thousand scrolls; the emperor ordered Secretariat Director Liu Guyang and others to arrange in order, removed duplicates and vulgar clutter; obtained correct imperial editions thirty-seven thousand-plus scrolls; placed them in the Eastern Capital's Xiuwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiaze Hall in the Western Capital held three hundred seventy thousand scrolls. The emperor ordered Secretariat Director Liu Guyang and others to collate the collection, strip out duplicates and rubbish, and select thirty-seven thousand authoritative volumes for the Xiuwen Hall in the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 又寫五十副本，簡為三品，分置西京、東都宮、省、官府，其正御書皆裝剪華淨，寶軸錦褾。

translations.literal: Also copied fifty duplicate sets, sorted into three grades, distributed to Western Capital, Eastern Capital palace, ministries, and government offices; the correct imperial books all were bound and trimmed splendid and clean, with jeweled rollers and brocade covers.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty duplicate sets were made, graded in three tiers, and distributed to the palaces, ministries, and offices of both capitals. The imperial editions were bound with jeweled rollers and brocade covers.

sentences.zh: 於觀文殿前為書室十四間，窗戶床褥廚幔，咸極珍麗，每三間開方戶，垂錦幔，上有二飛仙，戶外地中施機發。

translations.literal: Before Guanwen Hall built fourteen book chambers; windows, bedding, curtains—all extremely rare and splendid; every three chambers opened square doors, hung brocade curtains; above were two flying immortals; outside the doors in the ground mechanisms were installed.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Hall of Viewing Literature he built fourteen book chambers, furnished with windows, bedding, and curtains of the utmost luxury. Every three chambers shared a square doorway hung with brocade, above which stood two figures of flying immortals. Mechanisms were set into the floor outside each door.

sentences.zh: 帝幸書室，有宮人執香爐，前行踐機，則飛仙下，收幔而上，戶扉及廚扉皆自啟，帝出，則垂閉復故。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited the book chambers, palace women held incense burners; walking ahead they stepped on the mechanism—then the flying immortals descended, gathered the curtains and rose; door panels and cabinet doors all opened of themselves; when the emperor left, they hung closed and restored as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor entered, a palace woman bearing an incense burner stepped on the trigger. The flying immortals descended, drew up the curtains, and every door swung open by itself. When he left, everything closed and reset as before.

sentences.zh: 帝以戶口逃亡，盜賊繁多，二月，庚午，詔民悉城居，田隨近給。

translations.literal: The emperor, because household registers fled and bandits were numerous, in the second month on gengwu issued edict that commoners all dwell within cities; fields given according to proximity.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed by fleeing taxpayers and rampant banditry, the emperor in the second month, on gengwu day, ordered the people to live only within walled towns and assigned fields nearby.

sentences.zh: 郡縣驛亭村塢皆築城。

translations.literal: Commanderies, counties, post stations, villages, and stockades all built walls.
translations.idiomatic: Every commandery, county, post station, village, and stockade was ordered to build walls.

sentences.zh: 上谷賊帥王須拔自稱漫天王，國號燕；

translations.literal: Shanggu bandit chief Wang Xuba called himself King of Boundless Heaven; state name Yan;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuba of Shanggu proclaimed himself King of Boundless Heaven and styled his realm Yan;

sentences.zh: 賊帥魏刀兒自稱歷山飛：眾各十餘萬，北連突闕，南寇燕、趙。

translations.literal: Bandit chief Wei Dao'er called himself Flying Over Mount Li: each force over one hundred thousand; north linked with Tujue, south raided Yan and Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit chief Wei Dao'er styled himself Flying Over Mount Li; his followers numbered more than one hundred thousand, linking with the Turks in the north and raiding Yan and Zhao in the south.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖夢洪水沒都城，意惡之，故遷都大興。

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Gaozu dreamed floodwaters submerged the capital; he found it ill-omened, therefore moved the capital to Daxing.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Emperor Wen had dreamed that floodwaters submerged the capital—a sign he found ominous—and for that reason relocated the court to Daxing.

sentences.zh: 申明公李穆薨，孫筠襲爵。

translations.literal: Duke Shenming Li Mu died; grandson Yun inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Shenming Li Mu died, and his grandson Yun succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 叔父渾忿其吝嗇，使兄子善衡賊殺之，而證其從父弟瞿曇，使之償死。

translations.literal: Paternal uncle Hun resented his stinginess, had elder brother's son Shanheng assassinate him, and framed his younger paternal cousin Qutan, making him pay with his life.
translations.idiomatic: His paternal uncle Hun, resenting his stinginess, had his nephew Shanheng murder him and then framed his cousin Qutan to pay with his life.

sentences.zh: 渾謂其妻兄左衛率宇文述曰：「若得紹封，當歲奉國賦之半。」

translations.literal: Hun said to his wife's elder brother, Left Guard Commandant Yuwen Shu: "If I can succeed to the fief, each year I shall present half the state's tax revenue."
translations.idiomatic: Hun told his brother-in-law Yuwen Shu, commandant of the Left Guard: "If I can inherit the title, I will every year give you half the empire's tax revenue."

sentences.zh: 述為之言於太子，奏高祖，以渾為穆嗣。

translations.literal: Shu spoke on his behalf to the crown prince, memorialized Gaozu, and made Hun Li Mu's heir.
translations.idiomatic: Shu pleaded his case before the crown prince and memorialized Emperor Wen, who named Hun Li Mu's successor.

sentences.zh: 二歲之後，不復以國賦與述，述大恨之。

translations.literal: After two years he no longer gave Shu the state's tax revenue; Shu greatly resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later Hun stopped paying Shu his share of the tax revenue, and Shu came to hate him bitterly.

sentences.zh: 帝即位，渾累官至右驍衛大將軍，改封郕公，帝以其門族強盛，忌之。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne, Hun rose in office to Right Xiao Wei Grand General, was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Cheng; the emperor, because his clan was powerful, was jealous of him.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor's accession, Hun rose to grand general of the Right Xiao Wei Guard and was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Cheng; the emperor, wary of his clan's strength, grew suspicious of him.

sentences.zh: 會有方士安伽陀言「李氏當為天子」，勸帝盡誅海內凡李姓者。

translations.literal: It happened that the Daoist An Jiatuo said "The Li clan will become Son of Heaven," urging the emperor to execute every person surnamed Li within the seas.
translations.idiomatic: A Daoist named An Jiatuo then declared that "the Li will become Son of Heaven" and urged the emperor to slaughter every Li in the realm.

sentences.zh: 渾從子將作監敏，小名洪兒，帝疑其名應讖，常面告之，冀其引決。

translations.literal: Hun's nephew, Director of Palace Construction Min, whose childhood name was Hong'er—the emperor suspected the name matched the prophecy and often told him so to his face, hoping he would take his own life.
translations.idiomatic: Hun's nephew Min, director of palace construction, went by the childhood name Hong'er; the emperor suspected the name fulfilled the prophecy and repeatedly told him so to his face, hoping he would kill himself.

sentences.zh: 敏大懼，數與渾及善衡屏人私語；

translations.literal: Min was greatly afraid and repeatedly spoke in private with Hun and Shanheng behind closed doors;
translations.idiomatic: Min was terrified and repeatedly met in secret with Hun and Shanheng, speaking behind closed doors;

sentences.zh: 述譖之於帝，仍遣虎賁郎將河東裴會基表告渾反。

translations.literal: Shu slandered them to the emperor and also sent Tiger Guard Regiment Commander Pei Huiji of Hedong to memorialize that Hun was rebelling.
translations.idiomatic: Shu denounced them to the emperor and sent Pei Huiji of Hedong, a Tiger Guard regiment commander, to memorialize that Hun was plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 帝收渾等家，遣尚書左丞元文都、御史大夫裴蘊雜治之，案問數日，不得反狀，以實奏聞。

translations.literal: The emperor arrested Hun's household and sent Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing Yuan Wendu and Censor-in-Chief Pei Yun to investigate jointly; after questioning for several days they found no evidence of rebellion and reported the facts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor seized Hun's household and sent Yuan Wendu, left assistant director of the Masters of Writing, and Censor-in-Chief Pei Yun to investigate together; after days of interrogation they found no proof of rebellion and reported the truth.

sentences.zh: 帝更遣述窮治之，述誘教敏妻宇文氏為表，誣告渾謀因渡遼，與其家子弟為將領者共襲取御營，立敏為天子。

translations.literal: The emperor again sent Shu to exhaust the investigation; Shu coached and instructed Min's wife, Lady Yuwen, to write a memorial falsely accusing Hun of plotting, when crossing the Liao, to join with family members serving as generals in assaulting the imperial camp and making Min emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then sent Shu to press the case to the end; Shu coached Min's wife, Lady Yuwen, into writing a memorial falsely accusing Hun of plotting, during the crossing of the Liao, to join with kinsmen serving as generals in a surprise attack on the imperial camp and install Min as emperor.

sentences.zh: 述持入，奏之，帝泣曰：「吾宗社幾傾，賴公獲全耳。」

translations.literal: Shu brought it in and memorialized; the emperor wept and said: "My altars of soil and grain nearly toppled—it is thanks to you that I am preserved."
translations.idiomatic: Shu presented the memorial, and the emperor wept, saying: "My altars of soil and grain nearly fell—it is thanks to you that they stand intact."

sentences.zh: 三月，丁酉，殺渾、敏、善衡及宗族三十二人，自三從以上皆徙邊徼。

translations.literal: In the third month, on dingyou day, Hun, Min, Shanheng, and thirty-two clansmen were executed; all kin within three removes and above were exiled to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on dingyou day, Hun, Min, Shanheng, and thirty-two of their clansmen were put to death, and all relatives within three removes and above were banished to the border marches.

sentences.zh: 後數月，敏妻亦鴆死。

translations.literal: Several months later Min's wife was also poisoned to death.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later Min's wife was also killed by poison.

sentences.zh: 有二孔雀自西苑飛集寶城朝堂前，親衛校尉高德儒等十餘人見之，奏以為鸞。

translations.literal: Two peacocks flew from the Western Park and gathered before the hall of Baocheng; more than ten men including Personal Guard Commandant Gao Deru saw them and memorialized that they were phoenixes.
translations.idiomatic: Two peacocks flew from the Western Park and alighted before the hall at Baocheng; Gao Deru, a commandant of the Personal Guard, and more than ten others who saw them memorialized that they were phoenixes.

sentences.zh: 時孔雀已飛去，無可得驗，於是百僚稱賀。

translations.literal: At the time the peacocks had already flown away and nothing could be verified; thereupon the hundred officials offered congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: By then the peacocks had already flown away and nothing could be verified, yet the officials all offered congratulations.

sentences.zh: 詔以德儒誠心冥會，肇見嘉祥，擢拜朝散大夫，賜物百段，餘人皆賜束帛；

translations.literal: An edict said that Deru's sincere heart had mysteriously accorded with Heaven and he had first seen an auspicious omen; he was promoted to Court Gentleman for Dispersal and given a hundred rolls of goods, while the others were all given bolts of silk;
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared that Deru's sincere heart had mysteriously accorded with Heaven and that he had been first to witness an auspicious omen; he was promoted to court gentleman for dispersal and given a hundred rolls of goods, while the others all received bolts of silk;

sentences.zh: 仍於其地造儀鸞殿。

translations.literal: A Ceremonial Phoenix Hall was also built on that spot.
translations.idiomatic: and on that spot a Ceremonial Phoenix Hall was built.

sentences.zh: 己酉，帝行幸太原；

translations.literal: On jiyou day the emperor traveled to Taiyuan;
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou day the emperor set out for Taiyuan;

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，幸汾陽宮避暑。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, he visited Fenyang Palace to escape the heat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer he went to Fenyang Palace to escape the heat.

sentences.zh: 宮城迫隘，百官士卒布散山谷間，結草為營而居之。

translations.literal: The palace grounds were cramped; the hundred officials and soldiers were scattered among the valleys, making grass huts for camps to dwell in.
translations.idiomatic: The palace grounds were cramped, so officials and soldiers were scattered through the valleys and lived in camps of grass huts.

sentences.zh: 以衛尉少卿李淵為山西、河東撫慰大使，承製黜陟選補郡縣文武官，仍發河東兵討捕群盜。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of the Guard Li Yuan was made Pacification Commissioner of Shanxi and Hedong; by imperial commission he dismissed and promoted and selected and filled civil and military officials of commanderies and counties, and also sent Hedong troops to pursue and capture the bandit hosts.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan, vice minister of the guard, was appointed pacification commissioner of Shanxi and Hedong, empowered by imperial commission to appoint, dismiss, and fill civil and military posts in the commanderies and counties, and to dispatch Hedong troops against the bandit hosts.

sentences.zh: 淵行至龍門，擊賤帥母端兒，破之。

translations.literal: When Yuan reached Longmen he attacked bandit chief Mu Duan'er and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Yuan reached Longmen he attacked the bandit chief Mu Duan'er and routed him.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，乙丑，帝巡北塞。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, on yichou day, the emperor toured the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn, on yichou day, the emperor toured the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 初，裴矩以突厥始畢可汗部眾漸盛，獻策分其勢，欲以宗女嫁弟叱吉設，拜為南面可汗；

translations.literal: Earlier, Pei Ju, because Shibi Khan's followers were gradually growing strong, offered a plan to divide his power: he wished to marry an imperial clanswoman to his younger brother Chijishe and invest him as Southern Khan;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, seeing that Shibi Khan's following was steadily growing, Pei Ju proposed a plan to divide Turk power: marry an imperial clanswoman to Shibi's younger brother Chijishe and invest him as Southern Khan;

sentences.zh: 叱吉不敢受，始畢聞而漸怨。

translations.literal: Chiji did not dare accept; when Shibi heard of it he gradually grew resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Chiji did not dare accept the honor, and when Shibi heard of the scheme he grew steadily resentful.

sentences.zh: 突厥之臣史蜀胡悉多謀略，為始畢所寵任，矩詐與為互市，誘至馬邑下，殺之。

translations.literal: The Turk minister Shishu Huxi was full of stratagems and was favored and entrusted by Shibi; Ju feigned a mutual-trade market with him, lured him to below Mayi, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The Turk minister Shishu Huxi was a man of many stratagems and enjoyed Shibi's favor; Ju feigned a mutual-trade market, lured him beneath Mayi, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 遣使詔始畢曰：「史蜀胡悉叛可汗來降，我已相為斬之。」

translations.literal: He sent an envoy to announce to Shibi: "Shishu Huxi rebelled against the khan and came to surrender; I have already executed him on your behalf."
translations.idiomatic: He sent an envoy to tell Shibi: "Shishu Huxi rebelled against you and came over to us; I have already executed him on your behalf."

sentences.zh: 始畢知其狀，由是不朝。

translations.literal: Shibi knew the truth of the matter and from this no longer came to court.
translations.idiomatic: Shibi knew what had really happened and from then on ceased paying court.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，始畢帥騎數十萬謀襲乘輿，義成公主先遣使者告變。

translations.literal: On wuchen day Shibi led several hundred thousand horsemen planning to assault the imperial carriage; Princess Yicheng first sent an envoy to report the emergency.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen day Shibi led several hundred thousand horsemen in a planned assault on the imperial carriage; Princess Yicheng sent an envoy ahead to warn of the plot.

sentences.zh: 壬申，車駕馳入雁門，齊王暕以後軍保崞縣。

translations.literal: On renshen day the imperial carriage rushed into Yanmen; the Prince of Qi, Yang Liang, kept the rear guard at Guo county.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen day the imperial carriage raced into Yanmen; the Prince of Qi, Yang Liang, held the rear at Guo county.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，突厥圍雁門，上下惶怖，撤民屋為守禦之具，城中兵民十五萬口，食僅可支二旬，雁門四十一城，突厥克其三十九，唯雁門、崞不下。

translations.literal: On guiyou day the Turks besieged Yanmen; above and below were terrified; they tore down people's houses to make defensive equipment; in the city were one hundred fifty thousand soldiers and civilians, and provisions could barely last twenty days; of Yanmen's forty-one fortresses the Turks captured thirty-nine—only Yanmen and Guo did not fall.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou day the Turks besieged Yanmen; panic seized the court and city alike; houses were torn down for defensive materials; one hundred fifty thousand soldiers and civilians were inside, with provisions for barely twenty days; of the forty-one fortresses around Yanmen the Turks took thirty-nine—only Yanmen and Guo held out.

sentences.zh: 突厥急攻雁門，矢及御前；

translations.literal: The Turks pressed the attack on Yanmen, and arrows reached before the emperor;
translations.idiomatic: The Turks pressed hard on Yanmen, and arrows fell before the emperor himself;

sentences.zh: 上大懼，抱趙王杲而泣，目盡腫。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly afraid; he embraced Prince Zhao Yang Gao and wept until his eyes were wholly swollen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was terrified; he clutched Prince Zhao Yang Gao and wept until his eyes were swollen shut.

sentences.zh: 左衛大將軍宇文述勸帝簡精銳數千騎潰圍而出，納言蘇威曰：「城守則我有餘力，輕騎乃彼之所長，陛下萬乘之主，豈宜輕動！」

translations.literal: Left Guard Grand General Yuwen Shu urged the emperor to select several thousand elite horsemen to break out of the encirclement; Remonstrating Master Su Wei said: "If we hold the city we still have surplus strength; light cavalry is precisely their specialty; Your Majesty, lord of ten thousand chariots, how can you move lightly!"
translations.idiomatic: Left Guard Grand General Yuwen Shu urged the emperor to break out with a few thousand picked horsemen; Remonstrating Master Su Wei said: "While we hold the walls we still have strength to spare; light cavalry is exactly what they excel at—Your Majesty, lord of ten thousand chariots, must not take such a risk!"

sentences.zh: 民部尚書樊子蓋曰：「陛下乘危徼幸，一朝狼狽，悔之何及！

translations.literal: Minister of the Household Fan Zigai said: "Your Majesty took peril for a chance encounter; in one morning you would be in disarray—what use regretting it then!
translations.idiomatic: Minister of the Household Fan Zigai said: "Your Majesty courted danger for a whim; one morning of rout would leave regret too late!

sentences.zh: 不若據堅城以挫其銳，坐徵四方兵使入援。

translations.literal: Better to hold a strong city to blunt their edge and sit in place summoning troops from the four quarters to enter as relief.
translations.idiomatic: Better to hold this strong city, break their momentum, and summon relief from every quarter.

sentences.zh: 陛下親撫循士卒，諭以不復征遼，厚為勳格，必人人自奮，何憂不濟！」

translations.literal: Your Majesty should personally console and walk among the soldiers, proclaiming that the Liaodong campaign will not be resumed and setting generous merit rewards—then each man will exert himself of his own accord; why worry that it will not succeed!"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should walk among the troops in person, promise that the Liaodong campaign will not be resumed, and set generous rewards for merit—then every man will fight of his own will. What failure need we fear?"

sentences.zh: 內史侍郎蕭瑀以為：「突厥之俗，可賀敦預知軍謀；

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat Xiao Yu thought: "In Turk custom the khatun participates in advance knowledge of military plans;
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat Xiao Yu argued: "By Turk custom the khatun shares in military planning;

sentences.zh: 且義成公主以帝女嫁外夷，必恃大國之援。

translations.literal: Moreover Princess Yicheng, as the emperor's daughter married to a foreign tribe, must rely on the great state's support.
translations.idiomatic: moreover Princess Yicheng, the emperor's daughter given in marriage to a foreign tribe, must rely on the great state's support.

sentences.zh: 若使一介告之，借使無益，庸有何損。

translations.literal: If we send one messenger to tell her, even if it does no good, what harm could there be.
translations.idiomatic: Send one messenger to inform her—even if it avails nothing, what harm can it do?

sentences.zh: 又，將士之意，恐陛下既免突厥之患，還事高麗，若發明詔，諭以赦高麗、專討突厥，則眾心皆安，人自為戰矣。」

translations.literal: Also, in the minds of the soldiers and officers there is fear that once the Turk danger is escaped Your Majesty will again turn to Goguryeo; if a bright edict is issued proclaiming pardon for Goguryeo and exclusive pursuit of the Turks, then every heart will be reassured and each man will fight for himself."
translations.idiomatic: And the troops fear that once the Turk danger passes Your Majesty will turn again to Goguryeo; issue a clear edict pardoning Goguryeo and declaring war only on the Turks, and every heart will be steadied and each man will fight for himself."

sentences.zh: 瑀，皇后之弟也。

translations.literal: Yu was the empress's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was the empress's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 虞世基亦勸帝重為賞格，下詔停遼東之役。

translations.literal: Yu Shiji also urged the emperor to set heavy reward standards and issue an edict stopping the Liaodong service.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shiji also urged the emperor to set lavish rewards and issue an edict halting the Liaodong campaign.

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 帝親巡將士，謂之曰：「努力擊賊，苟能保全，凡在行陳，勿憂富貴，必不使有司弄刀筆破汝勳勞。」

translations.literal: The emperor personally toured the soldiers and said to them: "Strive to strike the bandits; if you can preserve the realm, all who stand in the ranks need not worry about wealth and rank—I shall certainly not let the clerks wield brush and ink to destroy your merit and toil."
