translations.idiomatic: The emperor walked among the troops and told them: "Fight hard against the enemy; if you preserve the realm, every man in the ranks need not worry about rank or reward—I will not let clerks wield their brushes to erase your merit."

sentences.zh: 乃下令：「守城有功者，無官直除六品，賜物百段；

translations.literal: He then ordered: "Those with merit in defending the city who have no office shall be directly appointed sixth rank and given a hundred rolls of goods;
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered: "Defenders with merit who hold no office shall be directly appointed to sixth rank and given a hundred rolls of goods;

sentences.zh: 有官以次增益。」

translations.literal: Those with office shall receive increases in rank step by step."
translations.idiomatic: those already in office shall receive successive promotions."

sentences.zh: 使者慰勞，相望於道，於是眾皆踴躍，晝夜拒戰，死傷甚眾。

translations.literal: Envoys sent to comfort them lined the roads one after another; thereupon the masses all leaped forward, resisting day and night, and the dead and wounded were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys bearing imperial comfort lined the roads, and the troops rallied, fighting day and night at heavy cost in dead and wounded.

sentences.zh: 甲申，詔天下募兵，守令競來赴難。

translations.literal: On jiashen day an edict ordered recruitment of troops throughout the realm; magistrates and prefects raced to come to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen day an edict called for troops empire-wide, and magistrates and prefects raced to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 李淵之子世民，年十六，應募隸屯衛將軍雲定興，說定興多繼旗鼓為疑兵，曰：「始畢敢舉兵圍天子，必謂我倉猝不能赴援故也。

translations.literal: Li Yuan's son Shimin, age sixteen, answered the call and was enrolled under Garrison Guard General Yun Dingxing; he advised Dingxing to deploy many relay banners and flags as a decoy force, saying: "Shibi dared raise troops to besiege the Son of Heaven because he thought we could not hastily come to relief.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan's son Shimin, sixteen years old, answered the call and served under Garrison Guard General Yun Dingxing; he advised Dingxing to stretch relay banners and flags as a decoy, saying: "Shibi dared besiege the Son of Heaven because he thought we could not reach him in time.

sentences.zh: 宜晝則引旌旗數十里不絕，夜則鉦鼓相應，虜必謂救兵大至，望風遁去。

translations.literal: By day you should draw banners and flags for tens of li without break; by night let gongs and drums answer one another—the barbarians will surely think relief troops have arrived in great force and flee at sight of the wind.
translations.idiomatic: By day stretch banners and flags for tens of li without end; by night answer with gongs and drums—the enemy will think a great relief army has come and flee at the first sign of wind.

sentences.zh: 不然，彼眾我寡，若悉軍來戰，必不能支。」

translations.literal: Otherwise they are many and we are few; if they bring their whole army to battle we surely cannot hold."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise they outnumber us; if their whole army comes to fight, we cannot stand."

sentences.zh: 定興從之。

translations.literal: Dingxing followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Dingxing did as he advised.

sentences.zh: 帝遣間使求救於義成公主，公主遣使告始畢云：「北邊有急。」

translations.literal: The emperor sent a secret envoy to beg rescue of Princess Yicheng; the princess sent an envoy to tell Shibi: "There is urgent trouble on the northern border."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a secret envoy to beg Princess Yicheng for rescue; the princess sent word to Shibi: "There is urgent trouble on the northern border."

sentences.zh: 東都及諸郡援兵亦至忻口；

translations.literal: Relief troops from the Eastern Capital and the various commanderies also reached Xinkou;
translations.idiomatic: Relief from the Eastern Capital and the commanderies also reached Xinkou;

sentences.zh: 九月，甲辰，始畢解圍去。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on jiachen day, Shibi lifted the siege and departed.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on jiachen day, Shibi lifted the siege and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 帝使人出偵，山谷皆空，無胡馬，乃遣二千騎追躡，至馬邑，得突厥老弱二千餘人而還。

translations.literal: The emperor sent men out to reconnoiter; the valleys were all empty and there were no Turk horses; he then sent two thousand horsemen in pursuit, reaching Mayi and capturing more than two thousand Turk weak and aged before returning.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent scouts out; the valleys were empty of Turk horses; he then sent two thousand horsemen in pursuit, reaching Mayi and bringing back more than two thousand Turk weak and aged.

sentences.zh: 丁未，車駕還至太原。

translations.literal: On dingwei day the imperial carriage returned to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei day the imperial carriage returned to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 蘇威言於帝曰：「今盜賊不息，士馬疲弊，願陛下亟還西京，深根固本，為社稷計。」

translations.literal: Su Wei spoke to the emperor, saying: "Now bandits do not cease; soldiers and horses are exhausted and worn—I wish Your Majesty would quickly return to the Western Capital, take deep root and solidify the foundation, and plan for the altars of soil and grain."
translations.idiomatic: Su Wei told the emperor: "Banditry still rages and men and horses are spent; Your Majesty should return quickly to the Western Capital, deepen your roots, and secure the foundation of the realm."

sentences.zh: 帝初然之。

translations.literal: The emperor at first agreed with this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at first agreed.

sentences.zh: 宇文述曰：「從官妻子多在東都，宜便道向洛陽，自潼關而入。」

translations.literal: Yuwen Shu said: "The attendant officials' wives and children are mostly in the Eastern Capital; it is convenient to go by a direct route to Luoyang and enter through Tong Pass."
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Shu said: "The attendant officials' wives and children are mostly in the Eastern Capital; it would be convenient to go straight to Luoyang and enter through Tong Pass."

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，壬戌，帝至東都，顧眄街衢，謂侍臣曰：「猶大有人在。」

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on renxu day, the emperor reached the Eastern Capital; he gazed about the streets and alleys and said to his attendants: "Still great people remain."
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on renxu day, the emperor reached the Eastern Capital; he looked about the streets and told his attendants: "There are still too many people here."

sentences.zh: 意謂向日平楊玄感，殺人尚少故也。

translations.literal: He meant that when he had earlier suppressed Yang Xuangan he had killed too few.
translations.idiomatic: He meant that when he had put down Yang Xuangan he had not killed enough.

sentences.zh: 蘇威追論勳格太重，宜加斟酌，樊子蓋固請，以為不宜失信，帝曰：「公欲收物情邪！」

translations.literal: Su Wei pursued the argument that the merit rewards were too heavy and should be moderated; Fan Zigai firmly petitioned, holding that faith should not be broken; the emperor said: "Do you, sir, wish to win popular sentiment!"
translations.idiomatic: Su Wei pressed his argument that the promised rewards were too lavish and should be scaled back; Fan Zigai pleaded hard that the throne must not break faith; the emperor said: "Are you trying to win popular favor!"

sentences.zh: 子蓋懼，不敢對。

translations.literal: Zigai was afraid and did not dare reply.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zigai was afraid and dared not answer.

sentences.zh: 帝性吝官賞，初平楊玄感，應授勳者多，乃更置戎秩：建節尉為正六品，次奮武、宣惠、綏德、懷仁、秉義、奉誠、立信等尉，遞降一階。

translations.literal: The emperor by nature was stingy with official rewards; when he first suppressed Yang Xuangan there were many who should have received merit, so he newly established military ranks: Jianjie Wei as regular sixth rank, then Fenwu, Xuanhui, Suide, Huairen, Bingyi, Fengcheng, Lixin, and other Wei, each descending one step.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was by nature stingy with official rewards; after suppressing Yang Xuangan many men deserved merit, so he created new military ranks: Jianjie Wei at regular sixth rank, then Fenwu, Xuanhui, Suide, Huairen, Bingyi, Fengcheng, Lixin, and the rest, each a step lower.

sentences.zh: 將士守雁門者萬七千人，至是，得勳者才千五百人，皆准平玄感勳，一戰得第一勳者進一階，其先無戎秩者止得立信尉，三戰得第一勳者至秉義尉，其在行陳而無勳者四戰進一階，亦無賜。

translations.literal: The soldiers who defended Yanmen numbered seventeen thousand; by this time those who received merit numbered only one thousand five hundred; all were measured by the standard for suppressing Xuangan: one who earned first merit in one battle advanced one rank; one without prior military rank received only Lixin Wei at most; one who earned first merit three times reached Bingyi Wei; one in the ranks without merit advanced one rank after four battles, and there were also no gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Seventeen thousand men had defended Yanmen; in the end only fifteen hundred received merit awards, all measured against the Xuangan standard: first merit in one battle meant one rank; men without prior military rank got no more than Lixin Wei; three first merits reached Bingyi Wei; men in the ranks without merit advanced one rank after four battles—and there were no gifts at all.

sentences.zh: 會仍議伐高麗，由是將士無不憤怨。

translations.literal: It happened that they were again debating campaigning against Goguryeo, and from this the soldiers and officers were all resentful and angry.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the court again debated war against Goguryeo, and the troops were filled with resentment.

sentences.zh: 初，蕭瑀以外戚有才行，嘗事帝於東宮，累遷至內史侍郎，委以機務。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xiao Yu, as an affinal relative with talent and conduct, had once served the emperor in the Eastern Palace and had risen in office to Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat, entrusted with critical affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xiao Yu, an able and upright affinal kinsman, had served the emperor in the Eastern Palace and risen to vice director of the Palace Secretariat, entrusted with critical affairs.

sentences.zh: 瑀性剛鯁，數言事忤旨，帝漸疏之。

translations.literal: Yu by nature was stiff and upright; he repeatedly spoke on affairs contrary to the imperial will, and the emperor gradually grew distant from him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was stiff-spined and outspoken; he repeatedly spoke against the emperor's wishes, and the emperor gradually distanced himself from him.

sentences.zh: 及雁門圍解，帝謂群臣曰：「突厥狂悖，勢何能為！

translations.literal: When the siege of Yanmen was lifted the emperor told the ministers: "The Turks were wildly rebellious—what could they have done!
translations.idiomatic: After the siege of Yanmen was lifted the emperor told his ministers: "The Turks were wildly insolent—what could they have done!

sentences.zh: 少時未散，蕭瑀遽相恐動，情不可恕！」

translations.literal: Before long they had not yet dispersed, yet Xiao Yu hastily alarmed and stirred them—such sentiment cannot be forgiven!"
translations.idiomatic: They had barely withdrawn when Xiao Yu rushed to spread alarm—such conduct cannot be forgiven!"

sentences.zh: 出為河池郡守，即日遣之。

translations.literal: He was sent out as prefect of Heguan and dispatched the same day.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as prefect of Heguan and ordered away the same day.

sentences.zh: 候衛將軍楊子崇從帝在汾陽宮，知突厥必為寇，屢請早還京師，帝不納，及解圍，帝怒曰：「子崇怯懦，驚動眾心，不可居爪牙之官。」

translations.literal: Guard General Yang Zichong accompanied the emperor at Fenyang Palace; knowing the Turks would surely raid, he repeatedly asked to return early to the capital; the emperor did not accept this; when the siege was lifted the emperor angrily said: "Zichong is cowardly and frightened the hearts of the masses—he cannot hold an office of fang and claw."
translations.idiomatic: Guard General Yang Zichong had accompanied the emperor at Fenyang Palace; foreseeing a Turk raid he repeatedly urged an early return to the capital, but the emperor would not listen; after the siege was lifted the emperor said in anger: "Zichong is a coward who shook the troops' hearts—he is unfit for a post among the emperor's claws and fangs."

sentences.zh: 出為離石郡守。

translations.literal: He was sent out as prefect of Lishi.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as prefect of Lishi.

sentences.zh: 子崇，高祖之族弟也。

translations.literal: Zichong was a clansman younger brother of Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Zichong was a younger clansman of Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 楊玄感之亂，龍舟水殿皆為所焚，詔江都更造，凡數千艘，制度仍大於舊者。

translations.literal: In Yang Xuangan's rebellion the dragon boats and water halls were all burned by him; an edict ordered them rebuilt at Jiangdu—several thousand vessels in all, their specifications still larger than the old ones.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xuangan's rebellion had burned the dragon boats and water halls; an edict ordered them rebuilt at Jiangdu—several thousand vessels in all, each larger than before.

sentences.zh: 壬申，盧明月帥眾十萬寇陳、汝。

translations.literal: On renshen day Lu Mingyue led a host of one hundred thousand to raid Chen and Ru.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen day Lu Mingyue led one hundred thousand men to raid Chen and Ru.

sentences.zh: 東海李子通，有勇力，先依長白山賊帥左才相，群盜皆殘忍，而子通獨寬仁，由是人多歸之，未半歲，有眾萬人。

translations.literal: Li Zitong of Donghai had courage and strength; he first attached himself to the bandit chief Zuo Caixiang of Changbai Mountain; the bandit hosts were all cruel, but Zitong alone was generous and humane, and from this many people joined him; in not half a year he had a host of ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zitong of Donghai was a man of courage and strength; he first joined the bandit chief Zuo Caixiang on Changbai Mountain; the outlaws were all cruel, but Zitong alone was generous and humane, and men flocked to him; in less than half a year he had ten thousand followers.

sentences.zh: 才相忌之，子通引去，渡淮，與杜伏威合。

translations.literal: Caixiang was jealous of him; Zitong led his men away, crossed the Huai, and joined Du Fuwei.
translations.idiomatic: Caixiang grew jealous; Zitong withdrew, crossed the Huai, and joined Du Fuwei.

sentences.zh: 伏威選軍中壯士養為假子，凡三十餘人，濟陰王雄誕、臨濟闞稜為之冠。

translations.literal: Fuwei selected strong warriors from the army and raised them as nominal sons—more than thirty in all—with Wang Xiong of Jiyin and Kan Ling of Linji foremost among them.
translations.idiomatic: Fuwei picked the strongest warriors in his army and adopted them as nominal sons—more than thirty in all—with Wang Xiong of Jiyin and Kan Ling of Linji at their head.

sentences.zh: 既而李子通謀殺伏威，遣兵襲之。

translations.literal: Before long Li Zitong plotted to kill Fuwei and sent troops to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Li Zitong plotted to kill Fuwei and sent troops against him.

sentences.zh: 伏威被重創墜馬，雄誕負之逃葭葦中，收散兵復振。

translations.literal: Fuwei was heavily wounded and fell from his horse; Xiongdan carried him and fled into the reeds, gathered the scattered troops, and revived their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Fuwei was gravely wounded and fell from his horse; Xiongdan carried him into the reeds, gathered the scattered troops, and rallied them again.

sentences.zh: 將軍來整擊伏威，破之；

translations.literal: General Lai Zheng attacked Fuwei and defeated him;
translations.idiomatic: General Lai Zheng attacked Fuwei and routed him;

sentences.zh: 其將西門君儀之妻王氏，勇而多力，負伏威以逃，雄誕帥壯士十餘人衛之，與隋兵力戰，由是得免。

translations.literal: The wife of his general Xi Men Junyi, Lady Wang, was brave and possessed great strength; she carried Fuwei and fled; Xiongdan led more than ten strong warriors to guard them and fought hard against Sui troops, and from this he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang, wife of his general Ximen Junyi, was brave and strong; she carried Fuwei to safety while Xiongdan led a dozen warriors to guard them and fought the Sui troops hand to hand, and so Fuwei escaped.

sentences.zh: 來整又擊李子通，破之，子通帥其餘眾奔海陵，復收兵得二萬人，自稱將軍。

translations.literal: Lai Zheng again attacked Li Zitong and defeated him; Zitong led his remaining host to flee to Hailing, again gathered troops and obtained twenty thousand men, and styled himself general.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Zheng then attacked Li Zitong and defeated him; Zitong fled to Hailing with his remnant force, raised troops again to twenty thousand, and styled himself general.

sentences.zh: 城父朱粲始為縣佐史，從軍，遂亡命聚眾為盜，謂之「可達寒賊」，自稱迦樓羅王，眾至十餘萬，引兵轉掠荊、沔及山南郡縣，所過□類無遺。

translations.literal: Zhu Can of Chengfù at first served as a county clerk, joined the army, then fled as an outlaw and gathered a host to become bandits; they called them the "Kedahan Bandits"; he styled himself King Garuda; his host reached more than one hundred thousand; he led troops in turn to plunder Jing, Mian, and the mountain-south commanderies and counties; wherever they passed, fowl, dogs, and the like left nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Can of Chengfù had begun as a county clerk, entered military service, then fled and gathered outlaws known as the Kedahan Bandits; he styled himself King Garuda and built a following of more than one hundred thousand; he swept through Jing, Mian, and the mountain-south commanderies and counties, leaving nothing alive wherever he passed—not even fowl or dogs.

sentences.zh: 十二月，庚寅，詔民部尚書樊子蓋發關中兵數萬擊絳賊敬盤陀等。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on gengyin day, an edict ordered Minister of the Household Fan Zigai to dispatch several tens of thousands of Guanzhong troops to attack the Jiang bandits Jing Pantuo and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on gengyin day, an edict ordered Minister of the Household Fan Zigai to dispatch tens of thousands of Guanzhong troops against the Jiang bandits Jing Pantuo and others.

sentences.zh: 子蓋不分臧否，自汾水之北，村塢盡焚之，賊有降者皆坑之。

translations.literal: Zigai did not distinguish good from bad; from north of the Fen River he burned every village stockade; bandits who surrendered were all buried alive.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zigai made no distinction between loyal and rebel; north of the Fen River he burned every village stockade, and every bandit who surrendered was buried alive.

sentences.zh: 百姓怨憤，益相聚為盜。

translations.literal: The common people resented and raged, and increasingly gathered together to become bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The people seethed with resentment and turned to banditry in ever greater numbers.

sentences.zh: 詔以李淵代之。

translations.literal: An edict made Li Yuan replace him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict replaced him with Li Yuan.

sentences.zh: 有降者，淵引置左右，由是賊眾多降，前後數萬人，餘黨散入它郡。

translations.literal: When there were those who surrendered, Yuan placed them at his side; from this many of the bandit host surrendered, several tens of thousands before and after; the remaining partisans scattered into other commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan kept surrendered men at his side, and bandits came over in droves—tens of thousands in all—while the remaining partisans scattered into other commanderies.
